## Exploration: C4 (issue #229) — close the post-cutover transitional window

### Current State (grounded findings, file:line)

**D1 — dualWrite config machinery (HIGHEST PRIORITY)**
- Sole runtime read site: `brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs:176` — `if (_loadConfig(root)?.memory?.dualWrite === true) { await dualWriteRecords(...) }` inside `share()` (engram.mjs:153-179). No other read call site in the whole repo (migrate-v1.mjs never reads it).
- Config load: `brain/scripts/lib/brain-config.mjs` `loadBrainConfig()`/`ensureBrainConfig()`; migrations registry at `brain/core/config-migrations.mjs` (6 entries, ALL additive via `{defaults}`, none via custom `migrate()`). `memory.dualWrite` added at migration `0.6.0` (config-migrations.mjs:86-99), default `false`.
- `mergeDefaults()` (`brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs:364-377`) can ONLY ADD missing keys — `if (!(key in out)) out[key] = defVal` — it structurally CANNOT remove a key. `migrateConfig()` (installer.mjs:422-442) only ever calls `mergeDefaults` or a custom `migrate(config, {mergeDefaults})` fn; every one of the 6 existing migrations uses the `defaults` (pure-additive) form. Zero precedent for a destructive/removal migration anywhere in the codebase.
- Real repo's own `brain.config.json` (repo root) has `"memory":{"dualWrite":true}` but `"schemaVersion":"0.3.0"` — STALE relative to the 0.6.0 migration that key belongs to. This proves `dualWrite:true` was set here by a MANUAL edit (the C2b-2 runbook's human keystroke), NOT via `migrateConfig`/`brain-upgrade.mjs`. `brain-upgrade.mjs` (lines 160-184) is the only code path that ever runs `migrateConfig`, and it is a manual/opt-in consumer command, not something CI or `npm test` runs against this repo's own config.
- Consequence for the decision: whichever mechanism C4 picks, THIS repo's own `brain.config.json` still needs a manual edit to actually remove/ignore the key locally — `config-migrations.mjs` changes only affect (a) fresh installs (`buildDefaultConfig()`, brain-config.mjs:119-142) and (b) downstream consumers who run `brain-upgrade`.

**D2 — pull/import path**
- `importMemory()` (engram.mjs:477-480) and `pullMemory()` (engram.mjs:513-533) are 100% chunk-based today: `execFileSync(engram, ["sync", "--import"])` — an opaque call into the engram binary that hydrates local engram from `.memory/chunks/*.jsonl.gz`.
- `importRecord()` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/engram-import.mjs:56-74`, shipped in C2b-1) is a PURE transform (record → engram observation shape) that is currently exercised ONLY by `engram-import.test.mjs` — it is NOT wired into `importMemory`/`pullMemory`/CLI `pull`/`import` at all. Confirmed via `engram.pull.test.mjs` (only mocked seams, no records path).
- Existing precedent for injecting a record into engram directly: `featureResume()`'s `_defaultEngramSave()` (engram.mjs:916-922) calls `execFileSync("engram", ["save", title, content, "--type", type, "--project", project, "--topic", topic])` — i.e. `engram save` is a real per-observation CLI verb already used elsewhere in this codebase. This is the natural mechanism to wire records-only import (read `.memory/records/*.jsonl` via `readRecordObservations`/`store.mjs`, transform via `importRecord()`, call `engram save` per record) instead of `engram sync --import` (chunks).
- `cli.mjs` VALID_OPS: `share|pull|import|index|reindex|migrate-v1|setup|feature-checkpoint|feature-resume` (cli.mjs:53-63); `pull`→`pullMemory`, `import`→`importMemory` via VERB_TO_EXPORT map (cli.mjs:210-215).

**D3/D4 — memory-gate chunks retirement**
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs:7,10-14,34-35,85,91` — memory-gate currently unions `readChunkObservations(cwd)` (`brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs:23-42`) and `readRecordObservations(cwd)` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/store.mjs:151-176`). Comment explicitly: "Retire the chunks-path once it is fully decommissioned (tracked for C4/D1)." Both readers are TRANSITIONAL by their own doc comments.
- **Cutover finding 7 CONFIRMED**: `_defaultChangedChunkFiles` (`engram.mjs:352-372`) runs `git status --porcelain --- .memory/chunks`, then `.split("\n").map(l => l.slice(3).trim()).filter(p => p.endsWith(".jsonl.gz"))` — NO filter on the porcelain status prefix (e.g. `D `/` D` for deletions also end in `.jsonl.gz` and pass the filter). Every returned path is then fed to `scrubChunkFile()` (`brain/scripts/memory/lib/secret-scrub.mjs:104-115`), which does `readFileSync(chunkPath)` at line 105 with NO existence guard — a deleted chunk path → ENOENT throw. This is a live bug in `scrubMaterializedChunks()` (engram.mjs:388-402), which the first post-cutover `share()` that deletes any chunk (e.g. cutover moved chunks to `legacy/`) will trip. Must be fixed in or before C4.

**D1 (round-trip) — format.mjs / provenance.mjs**
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`: `computeRecordId` (66-82, excludes `source` from hash per R3), `buildRecord` (99-107, R2 title fold).
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/provenance.mjs`: `renderProvenance`/`parseProvenance` (123-140 / 65-103) — the §4 prose grammar, already referencing `sdd/memory-format/c4-roundtrip-equality` as its own acceptance criterion (provenance.mjs top comment + engram-import.mjs:9 + engram-import.test.mjs:4-7).
- Existing round-trip scaffolding: `engram-import.test.mjs` ALREADY has full id-equality property tests including the EXACT issue-without-source pin the user described (lines 46-60: `roundTripId(record)` = `computeRecordId(exportObservation(importRecord(record)).record)` must equal `record.id`; asserts re-exported `source` becomes `'issue #305'` while original `record.source === undefined` — inert because `source` is hash-excluded). This is SYNTHETIC-fixture only.
- Gap for C4 D1: NO round-trip test exists yet against REAL committed data. Real records live at `.memory/records/2026-06.jsonl` (135 `@legacy` records from the cutover migration, of ~275 total) and `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl`. Precedent for a real-git-repo integration test style: `records-merge.integration.test.mjs` (builds temp repo, real git merge) — but that too uses synthetic records, not the actual committed store. C4 should add an integration test that reads the REAL `.memory/records/*.jsonl` (via `readRecordObservations`/`parseRecordLine`) and asserts `computeRecordId(exportObservation(importRecord(r)).record) === r.id` for every real record.

**D5 — openspec artifact convention**
`openspec/changes/issue-222-c2b2-cutover/` contains: `proposal.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`, `checkpoint-report.md`, `design.md`, `runbook.md`. The phase-order gate (`brain/scripts/vcs/phase-order-check.mjs`) requires `proposal.md` (line 326), `design.md` (327), `spec.md` OR `specs/*/spec.md` (329, 294), and `tasks.md` with checked items — all 4 must exist for any dir with implementation code, else Rule C fails. `issue-229-c4/` must mirror at minimum proposal/spec/design/tasks.md.

### Affected Areas
- `brain/core/config-migrations.mjs` — dualWrite removal/deprecation mechanism
- `brain/scripts/lib/brain-config.mjs`, `brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs` (mergeDefaults/migrateConfig) — additive-only constraint
- `brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs` — share()'s dualWrite gate (176), pullMemory/importMemory (477-533), _defaultChangedChunkFiles bug (352-372)
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/engram-import.mjs` — importRecord(), unwired into CLI pull/import
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/secret-scrub.mjs:104-115` — scrubChunkFile ENOENT risk on deleted paths
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs`, `brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs`, `brain/scripts/memory/lib/store.mjs` — memory-gate dual-source union to retire
- `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`, `provenance.mjs`, `engram-import.test.mjs` — round-trip contract, needs real-data integration test
- `.memory/records/2026-06.jsonl`, `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl` — real fixture data for D1's integration test

### Approaches — dualWrite removal (D1, the key decision)
1. **(a) schemaVersion-bump migration that REMOVES the key** — requires writing the FIRST-EVER non-additive `migrate(config, helpers)` function (all 6 existing migrations are pure `defaults`). Contradicts the file's own doctrine comment ("Migrations are ADDITIVE... NEVER overwrite... idempotent"). Also does not self-apply to THIS repo (own config already proven to need a manual edit regardless, since schemaVersion is stale at 0.3.0). Benefit: config is honestly clean going forward for downstream consumers running brain-upgrade.
   - Effort: Medium (new non-additive migration pattern + doctrine exception to justify + tests)
2. **(b) tolerate-and-ignore with deprecation warning** — delete the ONE read site (engram.mjs:176) or make it a no-op with a console.warn if `memory.dualWrite` is still present; leave the config key alone (or add a NEW additive migration that does nothing but document deprecation in a comment/description). Zero new migration mechanism needed, consistent with existing additive-only doctrine. Con: config key lingers forever in every consumer's file (minor clutter), and doesn't "close the window" as cleanly by the letter of D1's goal.
   - Effort: Low (single call-site change + optional warning)

### Recommendation
Favor **(b)**, with a twist: since dualWrite already flipped to `true` in production (this repo's `brain.config.json` confirms the real cutover happened), the code's job is simply to stop CONDITIONING on it — always dual-write is now just "the only write path" (records-only). The cleanest move is to delete the `if (dualWrite === true)` branch entirely and make `dualWriteRecords()` (or its replacement, unconditional record-write logic) run unconditionally in `share()`, then treat the config key as inert/deprecated (leave it in config-migrations.mjs history for provenance, optionally add a one-line description update noting "RETIRED at C4, no longer read"). This avoids inventing the repo's first destructive migration primitive for a key that has exactly one reader, while still fully "retiring" the gate from the code's perspective. If the team wants the config file itself to visibly shed the key for new installs, a narrow non-`defaults`-based migration entry could still be layered on later without blocking C4.

### Risks
- The `_defaultChangedChunkFiles` ENOENT bug (finding 7) is LIVE now that the real store has moved chunks to `legacy/` — any `memory:share` that also deletes a chunk will crash `scrubMaterializedChunks`. Should be fixed as part of D3/D4 or as a prerequisite hotfix.
- D2 (pull/import records-only) has NO existing wiring at all — it's greenfield, not a refactor. The engram binary's only documented per-observation write verb is `engram save` (used in featureResume); reusing that pattern for bulk records import needs a design decision on batching/performance for ~275+ records.
- D1's real-data round-trip test must handle the 135 `@legacy`-actor records from the cutover migration (source = "provenance unknown — migrated from engram chunk ...") as its dominant real-world case, not just synthetic pins.
- Removing/deprecating `dualWrite` while `run-check.mjs`'s memory-gate still unions both readers (D3/D4) means D1 and D4 are coupled — sequencing matters in tasks.md.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — sufficient grounded evidence exists for all 5 deliverables to author design.md and drive strict TDD. Key open question for the proposal/design phase: confirm with @csrinaldi whether config-key removal (option a) is a value worth paying doctrine-exception cost for, or whether option (b)'s "stop reading it" is acceptable given the key already served its purpose.

content:
**A2 (#231) GitLab governance CI — exploration gotcha: REQUIRED jobs can't stay pure bash on GitLab**

**What**: Mapped the exact surface A2 must mirror: GOVERNANCE_JOBS/REQUIRED_JOBS/DETECTION_JOBS (brain/scripts/vcs/governance-checks.mjs:24,33), the DETECTION two-case exit contract (ADR-0016 + issue-196-ci-context-impl/design.md Amendment 3), and ci-context.mjs's already-complete GitLab support (loadGitlabContext, ci-context.mjs:120-153).
**Why**: Grounding proposal/spec/design/ADR-draft/tasks for A2 (#231) — the GitLab CI pipeline that must consume ONLY ci-context.mjs, mirroring .github/workflows/governance.yml 1:1.
**Where**: brain/scripts/vcs/governance-checks.mjs, ci-context.mjs, phase-order-check.mjs, actor-check.mjs, brain-writes-reviewed.mjs, governance/run-check.mjs, .github/workflows/governance.yml, ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs, brain/core/managed-paths.mjs, brain/core/config-migrations.mjs, docs/inbox/PLAN-adapters-v3.md (§Track A2, untracked draft plan already in repo), ADR-0016.
**Learned**: Non-obvious structural gotcha — on GitHub, REQUIRED jobs `issue-link` and `diff-size` are pure bash embedded directly in governance.yml, reading `${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` / `.labels` from the Actions *event trigger payload* — they never call ci-context.mjs at all (only memory-gate/decision-gate go through run-check.mjs → loadContext()). GitLab CI has NO predefined-variable equivalent for MR description (confirmed via GitLab's own open feature request gitlab-org/gitlab#27598 — `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DESCRIPTION` does not exist), and `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_LABELS` freezes at pipeline-creation time (stale — ADR-0016 explicitly says do not use it). So A2's GitLab `issue-link` and `diff-size` jobs CANNOT be pure bash mirrors of the GitHub bash — they MUST route through a Node wrapper calling `loadContext()` (fresh API-fetched body/labels) to stay correct, unlike their GitHub siblings. This is a real design decision the A2 proposal/design phase must resolve explicitly (new CLI runner extending run-check.mjs vs bash-calls-node-prints-JSON), not an oversight to silently "fix" by copy-pasting GitHub's bash. Also: `governance.approvedLabel` config key does not exist yet (not in config-migrations.mjs) — PLAN-adapters-v3.md already scoped it as an A2 deliverable (configurable per-provider label, default `status:approved` GH / `status::approved` scoped GitLab); adding it requires an additive config-migrations.mjs entry (schemaVersion bump, brain/core/ = Tier-2/L6 human-review gate) but is NOT itself a brain/core *logic* change, just config schema. Repo's own brain.config.json is stale (schemaVersion 0.3.0 vs migrations up to 0.5.0) — unrelated pre-existing drift, not in A2 scope.

content:
**DOCTRINE — migration version numbers are content-identifiers, NEVER reused; the gap is honest record; retire-by-deletion includes the version slot (monotonic-forever)**

What: Human ruling at A2 (#231). A migration version number is a CONTENT-IDENTIFIER and is NEVER reused. Pinned when deciding the version for the new governance.approvedLabel config entry after C4 removed the never-shipped 0.6.0 (memory.dualWrite) entry.

RULING: governance.approvedLabel takes 0.7.0, NOT the freed 0.6.0 slot.

WHY: a reused 0.6.0 would name two indistinguishable states depending on WHEN it was applied — the exact ambiguity content-hashing exists to prevent. Critically, THIS repo ran under 0.6.0-dualWrite during the cutover window; that window's archaeology needs 0.6.0 to mean ONE thing. The gap at 0.6 is NOT a tolerable cost to avoid — it IS honest record: a hole in the migration sequence is the visible, log-readable mark of a retirement.

DOCTRINE (fixed for all future retirements): retire-by-deletion includes the version slot; the migration sequence is MONOTONIC-FOREVER (numbers only ever go up, gaps are permanent and meaningful). Extends [[architecture/config-key-retirement-doctrine]] (never-shipped keys retire by deletion) — now: their version number retires with them.

Where: brain/core/config-migrations.mjs (chain currently 0.1.0→0.5.0 after C4's 0.6.0 removal; A2 appends 0.7.0). Related: [[sdd/issue-229-c4/done]], [[sdd/issue-231-a2/kickoff]].

content:
**sdd/issue-231-a2/apply-progress**

**What**: CP-A2a review-remediation batch for issue #231 A2, on branch `feat/issue-231-a2-pr3` (final tranche, off merged `feature/v2.0.0`). Fixed M1 (MAJOR, closing-keyword vocabulary divergence), m2 (MINOR, issue-number extraction precedence), m4 (MINOR, drift-guard env vocabulary gap) with strict TDD RED→GREEN; documented m3 (MINOR, actor-check gh-hardcoded on GitLab) as a known gap in design.md without changing code, per the ruling. All prior A2 apply-progress (phases 1-5, commits 660b950/dc78d27/46fdea1/f332c41) remains complete and unaffected — this is a NEW commit on top, not a revision of those.

**Why**: CP-A2a PR review surfaced a real fail-closed parity divergence (`issueLink()`'s narrow 3-form closing-keyword regex vs GitHub bash's/actor-check.mjs's broad 9-form vocabulary — `Fixed #42` passed bash but failed the Node REQUIRED gate), an issue-number extraction precedence mismatch on slice targets (Node always resolved the closing ref first; bash resolves Part-of first), and a drift-guard blind spot (the negative-space env-var guard was never extended to cover the addendum's own new `DEFAULT_BRANCH`/`CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH` seam vars).

**Where** (commit 2ef6bdd, 8 files, 277 insertions/33 deletions):
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-ref-patterns.mjs` (NEW) — the ONE shared pure-constant module: `CLOSING_RE = /\b(close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\s+#(\d+)/i` (all 9 GitHub-documented forms, capture group 2 = issue number) and `CHAIN_RE = /\bpart\s+of\s+#(\d+)/i` (capture group 1 = issue number). No ci-context import — REQ-CIC-4 holds (pure evaluators may import a sibling pure-constants module; the guard is against the ci-context SEAM, not against unifying pure regex constants).
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.mjs` — deleted its own narrow local `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE`, now imports the shared broad pattern. `issueLink()`'s verdict WIDENS (accepts all 9 forms now, was 3). Reason string updated to describe the broader vocabulary while still containing "Part of" (existing test dependency).
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.test.mjs` — 5 new RED→GREEN tests: `Fixed #42`, `Close #10`, `Closed #3`, `Resolved #5`, `resolve #8` all → pass. 12/12 (was 7).
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs` — deleted local `CLOSING_NUM_RE`/`CHAIN_NUM_RE` duplicates, imports shared `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE`. `extractIssueNumber(body, closingRequired)` signature changed (now takes the already-computed `closingRequired` boolean from `requiresClosingKeyword(ctx)`): on a DEFAULT-branch target (`closingRequired===true`) only the closing pattern is consulted (mirrors bash's base==main branch, no Part-of fallback there); on a SLICE target, Part-of is tried FIRST then closing (mirrors bash's base!=main branch exactly — governance.yml:66-76). Docstring's false "SAME precedence as issueLink()" claim removed/corrected. The `!CLOSING_NUM_RE.test(...)` default-branch-policy check now uses the shared `CLOSING_RE`.
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.test.mjs` — 1 new m2 RED→GREEN test (body with BOTH `Closes #42` AND `Part of #7` on a slice target → asserts `fetchIssue` is called with `7`, not `42`, matching bash's Part-of-first slice precedence). 4 new M1 parity-table rows (`Fixed #N`, `close #N`, `Resolved #N` all PASS on both paths; PLUS the exact M1 case `Fixed #42` targeting the DEFAULT branch → PASS on both paths, the row that was previously impossible before the widen+precedence fix landed together). Truth-table header comment updated with a "VOCABULARY DIMENSION" note. 52/52 in this file (was 47 pre-fix, 4 new-row RED + 1 m2 RED = 5 failures confirmed before implementation).
- `brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs` — deleted its own `CLOSING_KEYWORD_RE`/`PART_OF_RE` (these were ALREADY the broad 9-form vocabulary, behaviorally identical to the new shared pattern), imports shared `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE` instead. Group-index references updated (`m[1]`→`m[2]` for `CLOSING_RE` since the shared regex's group 2 is the number, group 1 is the keyword; `CHAIN_RE`'s group 1 is unchanged). Pure refactor — 38/38 existing tests still pass unchanged (behavior-preserving, confirmed before AND after).
- `brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs` — `PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN` extended with `|DEFAULT_BRANCH|CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH` alternation. 1 new RED→GREEN test asserting the pattern now matches `process.env.DEFAULT_BRANCH` / `process.env.CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH`. 24/24 (was 23 pre-fix, 1 RED confirmed).
- `openspec/changes/issue-231-a2/design.md` — two new subsections: "Decision 2 ADDENDUM 2 (M1)" registers the precedent ("pure evaluator unchanged" / REQ-CIC-4 protects against refactor-drift, NOT against a ruled correctness fix — the evaluator accepted FEWER forms than the platforms honor, a pre-existing bug); "Known gap (m3)" documents `actor-check.mjs`'s `gh`-hardcoded fetch as an intentional DETECTION-only degrade-safe scope boundary, destined for CP-A2b/A3's provider-verb abstraction, NOT fixed in this slice.

**Learned**:
- REGEX STATEFULNESS GOTCHA discovered while writing the m4 RED test: `PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN` carries the `g` flag. `assert.match()` internally calls `RegExp#test()`, which on a GLOBAL regex mutates `lastIndex` across calls — asserting `assert.match('process.env.DEFAULT_BRANCH', PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)` then `assert.match('process.env.CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH', PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)` in the SAME test made the second assertion spuriously FAIL (lastIndex advanced past the shorter second string's length). Confirmed via a standalone repro before writing the real test. Fixed by using `String#match()` instead (which resets `lastIndex` to 0 internally on every call, per spec) — matching how the file's OWN pre-existing assertions already use `src.match(PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)`, never `assert.match`/`.test()`, on this specific global regex. Reusable gotcha: never `assert.match()` (or raw `.test()`) a shared global-flagged regex object across multiple assertions in the same test — use `String#match()` or a fresh `RegExp` instance instead.
- The M1 fix required touching BOTH `issue-link.mjs` (the pure evaluator's pass/fail check) AND `run-check.mjs` (its own separately-duplicated `CLOSING_NUM_RE` used for the default-branch closing-keyword POLICY check and issue-number extraction) — widening only one would have left the other half of the parity gap open. The exact M1 parity-table row (`Fixed #42` to default branch) only goes green when both fixes land together; it was used as the integration-level proof, not just the unit-level `issueLink()` tests.
- `CLOSING_RE`'s shared regex group indices differ from what each of the three original files used to use (`issue-link.mjs`'s old version had NO capture groups at all — boolean-only; `run-check.mjs`'s old `CLOSING_NUM_RE` had the number at group 1 via a non-capturing keyword group; `actor-check.mjs`'s old `CLOSING_KEYWORD_RE` also had the number at group 1). The new shared regex captures the KEYWORD at group 1 (needed nowhere directly, but keeping it capturing rather than non-capturing was a deliberate design choice for readability) and the NUMBER at group 2 — every importer needing the number was updated to reference `match[2]`, not `match[1]`.
- Verified via `git show --stat` on the sibling C4 review-fix commit (`f7b5ae0`, "fix(memory): address C4 review") that review-remediation commits do NOT touch `tasks.md` — precedent followed here: `tasks.md` left untouched (these findings were never task-list items, they're PR-review findings).

Full `npm test`: 1132/1132 pass, 0 failures (baseline before this batch was 1121; +11 new tests: 5 issue-link.test.mjs + 5 run-check.test.mjs (4 parity rows + 1 m2 precedence test) + 1 ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs). `repo:check` and `brain:nav` both clean. Commit `2ef6bdd` "fix(governance): unify closing-keyword vocabulary (9 forms, shared) + issue-num precedence + drift-guard env (A2 CP-A2a review) (#231)" on branch `feat/issue-231-a2-pr3`, ONE commit, no push, no PR (per instructions). `brain/core/` untouched this batch (no L6 brain-writes-reviewed gate engagement needed). `.memory/` and `docs/inbox/PLAN-adapters-v3.md` deliberately excluded from staging.

content:
**PATTERN — chained PRs: sequential tranches against the feature branch (no separate tracker branch); split by budget, one slice/design/checkpoint**

What: The chained-PR convention, RE-CAPTURED as a valid record (type: pattern). It was one of two valuable rules lost when a prior migration rejected it as type:preference ("chained PRs use a tracker/history branch"). Re-captured here at A2 (#231) — its natural moment — and UPDATED to how the chain works today.

**How chained PRs work now (updated form):**
- When a single approved slice's counted diff exceeds the 400 budget, SPLIT into sequential tranches — do NOT size:exception (budget is a planning forcing-function; a forecast wrong by ~2x is corrected by splitting). Exception is reserved for MANDATED ATOMICITY (the #216 precedent), not for a linear dependency chain.
- **Sequential, NOT stacked, against the feature branch directly:** PR-1 targets feature/v2.0.0 and merges → PR-2 opens off the UPDATED feature/v2.0.0 → merges → PR-3. No separate tracker/history branch (that was the old rejected form).
- ONE slice / ONE design / ONE checkpoint delivered in N tranches by budget. All PRs `Part of #<issue>`; NO new issues per tranche (contrast the C2 re-split, which separated deliverables of different evidentiary nature and earned their own issues).
- Each tranche gets an express review focused on its slice; the FINAL checkpoint verdict (e.g. CP-A2a) is issued on the LAST PR, read against the full accumulated tree so the cross-tranche story (here: parity YAML↔run-check↔drift-guard) is verified whole.
- Split boundaries follow the natural dependency order (each tranche depends only on already-merged ones).

Precedent instance: A2 #231 → PRs #232 (tranche 1), then 2, then 3.

content:
**PATTERN — build the parity truth-table BEFORE implementing: enumerating the reference's input dimensions surfaces divergences in design (caught 2 A2 bugs pre-test)**

What: A ratified methodological pattern (human ruling at CP-A2a). When porting behavior from a reference implementation to a new transport (e.g. GitHub bash governance → GitLab Node run-check), BUILD THE PARITY TRUTH-TABLE FIRST — encode the reference's verdict for every input dimension BEFORE implementing the port. Constructing the table forces you to ENUMERATE the reference's input dimensions, and that enumeration surfaces divergences the implementation would otherwise hide silently.

Evidence: the A2 (#231) issue-link parity table caught TWO real divergences as DESIGN artifacts, before they ran as tests:
1. **Base-branch conditionality** — GitHub bash requires a closing keyword on the default branch; the ported pure issueLink() was base-branch-blind (would false-pass "Part of #N" to the default branch). Surfaced while scoping the table's dimensions.
2. **Closing-keyword vocabulary (M1)** — the pure evaluator accepted only closes|fixes|resolves while GitHub bash + actor-check honor all 9 forms (Fixed #42 diverged). Surfaced when the review analyzed the table's parity claim across the vocabulary dimension.

Both were verdict divergences (not transport differences) that a name-parity-only or a "port then test the happy path" approach would have missed. The parity table is a DESIGN tool that happens to also be a test.

Rule: parity ports write the truth-table (reference verdict × every input dimension) first; treat missing dimensions as the highest-risk unknowns. Related: [[sdd/issue-231-a2/kickoff]], [[pattern/chained-prs-sequential]].

**FINDING #13 (CP-A2b live): local-checks failed because node:20 lacks glob support in `node --test` (needs 21+); fix = node:22 in the fragment + drift-guard should pin the image version**

What: CP-A2b live — `local-checks` failed on BOTH MRs (NOT shallow-clone as first suspected). Root cause: the CI image is node:20, and `node --test "brain/scripts/**/*.test.mjs"` GLOB support landed in Node 21+. On node:20 the glob is not expanded → "Could not find .../brain/scripts/**/*.test.mjs" → exit 1.

Fix: pin **node:22** in the GitLab fragment (brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml). Design evaluation (reviewer to rule): (1) global `default: image: node:22` vs per-job `image:` — global default is one place, all 8 jobs inherit (recommended); (2) the DRIFT-GUARD should ASSERT the image version (node:22+) — a consumer who downgrades to node:20 breaks silently, the SAME class as the allow_failure-iff-DETECTION lock. The guard covers everything it guards.

Related — #12 REFINED (decision now evidence-resolved): MR-A's log proved the GitLab LOADER already speaks DIRECT API v4 (fetch + VCS_TOKEN — read the MR body live, ~9s network call, and emitted the message with M1's WIDE closing-keyword vocabulary — the adversarial-review fix visible in production). So the pipeline ALREADY runs the correct pattern; gitlab.mjs `issueView`'s glab dependency is the inconsistency. Option (b) — migrate issueView + all CI-consumed GitLab verbs to direct fetch against CI_API_V4_URL with VCS_TOKEN — is no longer a lean, it is UNIFYING on the proven mechanism (ci-context defaultFetchMr). glab → local interactive only.

RE-RUN mechanics for the runbook (important): a GitLab MR pipeline runs the SOURCE branch tree (refs/merge-requests/N/head), so a retry alone re-runs the OLD fragment. After merging the micro-fix + re-pushing the mirror, the two test/* branches must be UPDATED (merge feature/v2.0.0 into each + push) so the MRs re-evaluate against the corrected tree.

Delivery: micro-fix PR with #12 + #13 together, Part of #231, express. #12's fix rests on the glab-ENOENT diagnosis — CONTINGENT on the MR-B issue-link log: if it confirms ENOENT, nothing changes; if it shows something else, STOP and report before shipping the #12 part. Where: brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml, brain/scripts/vcs/providers/gitlab.mjs (issueView), brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context.mjs (defaultFetchMr = the template), ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs. **What**: Fixed CP-A2b live-validation findings #12 and #13 on branch fix/issue-231-cp-a2b-ci-portability. Commit 6965052.

**Why**: Live validation against the gitlab.com mirror surfaced two CI-portability bugs in the GitLab governance pipeline fragment (brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml): (#13) `node --test "brain/scripts/**/*.test.mjs"` needs Node 21+ glob expansion, but the fragment pinned node:20 per-job → local-checks failed "Could not find ..."; (#12) providers/gitlab.mjs's issueView shelled out to the `glab` CLI, absent from the node:22 image, crashing the REQUIRED issue-link gate's defaultFetchIssue on every MR (an INFRA trigger masquerading as a governance failure).

**Where**:
- `brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml` — removed per-job `image: node:20` (8x), added ONE global `default: image: node:22` block.
- `brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs` — new test asserting the global node:22+ pin exists and no job carries its own `image:` line (downgrade-to-node:20 turns RED, sanity-verified); fixed `extractGitlabJobNames` to exclude the new reserved `default:` top-level key (would have false-positived as a 9th "job").
- `brain/scripts/vcs/gitlab-api.mjs` (NEW) — shared PURE GitLab REST v4 fetch helper `gitlabApiFetch({apiBase, token, proxyUrl, path, fetchImpl})`. No env reads inside — not a GATE_FILE member by construction.
- `brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context.mjs` — extracted `gitlabApiConfig(deps)` export (sole sanctioned resolver of {apiBase, token, proxyUrl} from CI_API_V4_URL/VCS_TOKEN/HTTPS_PROXY); refactored `defaultFetchMr` to consume the shared `gitlabApiFetch` helper (no behavior change, REQ-CIC-5 tests stay green).
- `brain/scripts/vcs/providers/gitlab.mjs` — `issueView` migrated from `runJson('glab', ['api', ...])` to `gitlabApiFetch` with `{apiBase, token, proxyUrl, fetchImpl}` threaded in as parameters (never reads process.env.CI_API_V4_URL directly — gitlab.mjs is a GATE_FILE). Defaults preserve local/non-CI callers (ticket-start.mjs, brain-start.mjs): apiBase defaults to public gitlab.com, token defaults via existing `vcsToken(PROVIDER)`. issueList/mrList/etc. NOT migrated (local-interactive glab session auth, A3 territory).
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs` — `defaultFetchIssue(ctx)` now calls `gitlabApiConfig()` (imported from ci-context.mjs) and threads `{apiBase, token, proxyUrl}` into `vcs.issueView(...)`. github.mjs's issueView ignores the extra keys, so this is safe for both providers.

- The drift-guard's PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN regex scans full file source text, including comments/JSDoc — writing `process.env.CI_API_V4_URL` literally in a docstring (even to describe what NOT to do) trips the guard. Had to reword documentation to say "the GitLab API base URL pipeline var" instead of the literal env-var-prefixed string, in both gitlab.mjs and run-check.mjs.
- `extractGitlabJobNames` in ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs matches any zero-indent `word:` YAML key as a "job name" (only excludes leading-dot template keys) — introducing a global `default:` top-level key required extending its exclusion list, otherwise the existing GOVERNANCE_JOBS-equality test would have false-positived on "default" as an unrecognized 9th job.

content:
**FINDING #14 (CP-A2b re-run): defaultFetchIssue calls getVcs() with no args → resolves provider from CONFIG (github), ignoring runtime ctx.provider (gitlab) → GitLab job ran `gh api` on a GitLab issue**

What: CP-A2b MR-B re-run (description corrected) surfaced a config-vs-runtime provider bug. The self-diagnostic message earned itself AGAIN: the log literally said "gh api repos/csrinaldi/brain/issues/1 failed (status null)" — the GitLab job fetched the issue with the GITHUB provider. Root cause: `defaultFetchIssue` (run-check.mjs:169) calls `getVcs()` with NO args → `resolveProviderName` (vcs/cli.mjs:32) resolves `env.VCS_PROVIDER || config.vcs.provider` = github (the fragment sets no VCS_PROVIDER), IGNORING the runtime-detected `ctx.provider` (gitlab, from ci-context detectCi). So #236's direct-API GitLab issueView was READY but NEVER SELECTED — the dispatcher picked github → ran `gh`.

Fix (Part of #231, express): `defaultFetchIssue` selects the provider from `ctx.provider`. Semantics: the referenced issue lives on the platform HOSTING the MR (mirror's #1 is a GitLab issue; same for SCIT). Add an explicit `provider` override to `getVcs`/`resolveProviderName` (precedence: explicit provider > VCS_PROVIDER env > config.vcs.provider), and call `getVcs({ provider: ctx.provider })`. Backward-compatible (the other 5 callers don't pass it). Test: ctx.provider 'gitlab' → loads gitlab, NEVER spawns gh (extend the anti-spawn guard to the DISPATCH level, not just the fetch).

AUDIT (config-vs-runtime class): of 6 getVcs() call sites, ONLY run-check.mjs:169 is a CI-gate path → the only one with this bug. The other 5 (day-start, ticket-start, brain-audit, tracker-board, project-status) are LOCAL commands running in the repo's own config context, where config.vcs.provider IS correct. Fix scoped to defaultFetchIssue.

Live validation from this re-run (all GOOD): node:22 ran in both jobs (#13 confirmed live); MR-B body read via LIVE API with the `Closes` found (loader end-to-end ✓); the fetch-issue fail-closed message named the TOOL and STATUS. The blind-diagnosis cycle is officially dead — the self-diagnostic message pattern has now paid off on THREE consecutive findings (#12 case-A, #14 wrong-provider). Where: brain/scripts/vcs/cli.mjs (getVcs/resolveProviderName), brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs (defaultFetchIssue). Related: [[findings/12-gitlab-issueview-glab-ci]], [[pattern/parity-table-before-implementing]].

content:
**A2 CP-A2b MIRROR PHASE VALIDATED (gitlab.com): full governance chain green live; meta-lesson — infra premieres fail in LAYERS, the self-diagnostic message turns each into a 1-hour fix**

What: CP-A2b MIRROR PHASE VALIDATED on the public gitlab.com mirror (reviewer verdict, 3rd run). MR-compliant = 8/8 Passed — issue-link GREEN exercised the ENTIRE chain in one line: live-API MR body → M1 wide closing-keyword vocab → runtime-provider dispatch (#14) → issueView over direct API v4 (#12) → resolver `:`→`::` → issue's `status::approved` → base-branch addendum on the default branch. MR-non-compliant = issue-link Failed + the other 7 Passed → surgical red + mechanical block via "Pipelines must succeed" = rung 1 GitLab OPERATIONAL.

The layers surfaced across the iteration (each run peeled one):
1. include: — the fragment resolved (ADR-0018 opt-in dogfooded live).
2. IMAGE — #13: node:20 lacks glob in `node --test` → node:22.
3. LOADER/body — case A (operator error: literal `#<IID>` placeholder) proved the ci-context loader reads the MR body via live API; the self-diagnostic message (null-body vs no-ref) discriminated it.
4. DISPATCH — #14: defaultFetchIssue used config provider (github) not runtime ctx.provider (gitlab) → ran `gh` on a GitLab issue.

META-LESSON (ratified): infrastructure PREMIERES fail in LAYERS — an include is not "done" when it resolves; each layer (image, context, dispatch, verb transport) is a separate first-contact failure. The SELF-DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGE (name the tool + status + which stage failed) is what converts each layer from a blind-guess cycle into a ~1-hour fix. It paid off on THREE consecutive findings (#12 case-A, #14 wrong-provider, and the null-body/no-ref split). Corollary: injectable-seam test suites prove LOGIC but NOT that the default impl runs in the target environment — a live smoke against a real (even public-mirror) instance is irreplaceable for infra premieres.

Status: A2 fixture + mirror validated. #231 STAYS OPEN — remaining: CP-A2b SCIT phase (env-specifics smoke: CE version, corporate proxy, self-hosted runners, new endpoint) when the human restores access. That is the ONLY thing between A2 and total closure. Mirror MRs + test/* branches can be closed/deleted (evidence captured in cp-a2b-runbook.md Results). **What**: SDD design for A3 (#239) — GitLab provider verbs + provider-agnostic `labelEvents` contract verb. Closes two A2 debts: the `m3` `gh`-hardcoded actor-check fetch and the `prView`/`mrCreate` GitLab stubs.

**Why**: On GitLab runners the actor-check degraded to a permanent `warn` (no `gh` binary → ENOENT → catch → warn) so it could never DETECT self-approval; and A2 left `prView`/`mrCreate` as stubs.

**Where**: openspec/changes/issue-239-a3/{proposal,spec,design,tasks}.md. **Learned / 6 encoded decisions**:
1. `labelEvents` CONTRACT verb (NOT `resourceLabelEvents`), dispatched on runtime `ctx.provider` via `getVcs({provider})` (finding #14 pattern from run-check.mjs:167-177). Normalized shape `[{actor:{login},action:'add'|'remove',label,at}]|null`, ascending order so evaluateActor's "last=most recent" holds. Pure `evaluateActor` UNCHANGED; `filterLabeledEvents` becomes shared post-filter over normalized `action`.
2. GitHub `labelEvents` STAYS on `gh` CLI (RULED, human-flagged) — extracted behavior-preserving from actor-check (proof: actor-check.test.mjs unchanged), preserving load-bearing `--paginate`. Only GitLab goes direct-API (glab absent from CI image). `gh`-in-Actions explicitly ACCEPTABLE; no `githubApiFetch` invented (scope creep). Asymmetry is honest.
3. DETECTION-class honesty: GitLab actor-check now EVALUATES (self-approval → same `fail` as GitHub, REQ-L5-1) but gate CLASS stays DETECTION/`allow_failure` — REPORTS, never BLOCKS. No wording may read "blocks".
4. Fixture provenance: committed recording script hits real APIs once (GitLab live mirror; GitHub this repo), stamps each JSON `endpoint+date`; synthetic cases marked `DERIVED`; recorded-vs-derived always visible (lesson #12).
5. ONE shared parameterized contract suite over both providers; parity = identical assertions; injected fixture transport, no live network.
6. Unify contract in all 3 disagreeing places (vcs-contract.md + cli.mjs VERBS + exports) — in-scope. vcs-contract.md under brain/core/ = L6 boundary, expected PASS+warn (FIFTH such slice).

**Split**: Honest forecast >400 (~560-780; contract suite + recorded JSON fixtures are drivers) → 3 SEQUENTIAL chained PRs into feature/v2.0.0, all `Part of #239`, no new issues. PR-1 labelEvents+m3+refactor; PR-2 prView/mrCreate un-stub; PR-3 contract suite + fixture infra. CP-A3a verdict on PR-3 (full tree). CP-A3b live smoke DEFERRED to SCIT phase.

**sdd/governance/proposal**

## Proposal: governance — v2 (floor + audit + golden path)

**Intent:** Enforce brain's four load-bearing invariants as far as the environment allows and make compliance the path of least resistance. Core principle: enforce observable OUTPUTS wherever a gate can fail-closed; guide irreducible JUDGMENT with in-context docs. Never claim to enforce what cannot be mechanically verified.

**4 invariants:** (1) no merge without approved ticket, (2) no PR >400 changed lines without `size:exception`, (3) memory dumped before close, (4) ADR for every decision.

**Honest boundary:** a fully tool-independent HARD guarantee does not exist on SaaS — the chokepoint at merge is platform-owned. What IS universal: a default-on local floor + post-hoc audit.

**Architecture — three composed layers (v2 model):**
- Floor (always-on, tool-independent): generic checks library (node/git) + client-hook suite (commit-msg/pre-commit/pre-push) + brain:audit (re-verify merged history). The universal backbone.
- Hard gate (additive, capability-aware): VCS adapter — protectBranch() returns {enforced, reason, remedy}, never crashes; capabilities() probed not hardcoded. Platform enforcement where the tier allows.
- Golden path: self-gating brain verbs (brain:start/check/save/ship/next) unifying human + agent.

**5 slices:**
- S1 Foundation ✅ Done — ADR-0014, PR template, governance.ignoreList, managed-paths
- S2 Platform CI ✅ Done — governance.yml issue-link + diff-size (one additive adapter, not the universal guarantee)
- S3 Capability-aware adapter — protectBranch → {enforced,reason,remedy}, capabilities(), brain:governance status
- S4 The floor — generic checks library (diff-size, issue-link, adr-presence, memory-presence) + client-hook suite (commit-msg/pre-commit/pre-push) + brain:audit (re-verify merged history, the universal teeth)
- S5 Golden path — brain:start/check/save/ship/next verbs + --no-verify policy (repo:check prohibited-ref + harness PreToolUse hook)
- Phase 3 deferred: GitLab/Bitbucket protectBranch + pre-receive, rulesets, full session_summary check

**Non-goals:** full Inv-3 session_summary check (engram JSONL schema unconfirmed + no session/{issue} convention — Phase 3); enforcing capture quality; enforcing "sliced well"; GitLab protectBranch; GitHub rulesets; .github/** as managed glob.

**Where:** openspec/changes/governance/proposal.md (this topic — v2 reshape). Files: all prior + scripts/governance/checks/{diff-size,issue-link,adr-presence,memory-presence}.mjs + scripts/hooks/commit-msg + scripts/hooks/pre-commit + scripts/brain-audit.mjs + scripts/brain-{start,check,save,ship,next}.mjs + harness PreToolUse config.

**sdd/governance/design**

## Design: governance — v2 (floor + additive hard gate + golden path)

**Canonical design doc:** docs/inbox/workflow-governance-layer.md

**Architecture:** generic checks library → composed at three points:
1. Floor (always-on): client hooks (commit-msg/pre-commit/pre-push via core.hooksPath) + brain:audit (re-verify merged history). The floor does NOT fall back to the adapter; they compose independently.
2. Hard gate (additive): VCS adapter — protectBranch() returns {enforced:true} or {enforced:false, reason, remedy}; capabilities() probes the API (never hardcodes matrix); brain:governance status reports per-consumer.
3. Golden path: brain:start/check/save/ship/next self-gating verbs.

**Slices:**
- S1 ✅ Done: ADR-0014, PR template, governance.ignoreList migration, two managed paths
- S2 ✅ Done: governance.yml issue-link + diff-size (one additive adapter, CI-conditional)
- S3: protectBranch → {enforced,reason,remedy}; capabilities() via API probe; brain:governance status; GOVERNANCE_JOBS stays ['issue-link','diff-size'] (NO new CI jobs in S4)
- S4: Generic checks library (scripts/governance/checks/ — diff-size.mjs, issue-link.mjs, adr-presence.mjs, memory-presence.mjs); hook suite (new commit-msg + pre-commit; extend pre-push); brain:audit (scripts/brain-audit.mjs — git log --merges + 4 checks per merge + FAIL attribution)
- S5: brain:start/check/save/ship/next scripts; --no-verify prohibited in check-config + harness PreToolUse hook

**Key design decisions:**
- GOVERNANCE_JOBS stays ['issue-link','diff-size'] — S4 does NOT add memory-gate or decision-gate as CI jobs (v1 pattern). Checks move to the floor (hooks + audit) not more CI jobs.
- protectBranch() never throws/crashes — returns {enforced,reason,remedy} shape always.
- capabilities() PROBED not hardcoded — the tier matrix rots; probe + cache the 403/result.
- brain:audit verifies OUTCOME (merged history), forge-proof, attributes violations to SHA.
- The --no-verify policy: prohibited-ref in repo:check (tool-independent) + harness hook (agent-layer) + audit catches what slips through.

**File changes (new vs v1):** Removed: memory-gate and decision-gate YAML jobs from governance.yml. Added: scripts/governance/checks/*.mjs, scripts/hooks/commit-msg, scripts/hooks/pre-commit, scripts/brain-audit.mjs, scripts/brain-{start,check,save,ship,next}.mjs, scripts/brain-governance-status.mjs, harness PreToolUse config.

**Where:** openspec/changes/governance/design.md

## Key Design Decisions (S5)

### S5.1 — Branch creation is local git (not VCS API)
Branch creation uses `git checkout -b` directly (local git op, always works). The VCS adapter is only used for issue metadata (issueView). This is more honest than going through the API for a local branch.

### S5.2 — brain:check uses dependency injection
All 4 checks + npmTest + repoCheck are passed as injectable fns. CLI wires real implementations. Tests use stubs. No process.exit in the exported function — only in the CLI guard.

### S5.5 — brain:next state machine priorities
1. no-branch (main/master/dev/develop/release/*) → brain:start
2. open-pr (PR exists for current headBranch) → monitor
3. no-memory (no uncommitted .memory/) → brain:save
4. checks-failing (repo:check exits non-zero) → brain:check
5. ready (everything ok) → brain:ship

Non-working branches: only main/master/dev/develop/release/* are treated as non-working. feature/* and gov/* are allowed as working branches (issue-number branches like feature/42-slug are working).

### S5.6 — no-verify-bypass rule placement
Rule added to brain/project/check-refs-rules.mjs (NOT brain/core/), keeping project-specific rules separate from core. onlyExt limits to .mjs/.js/.ts/.sh. Hook files (no extension) are naturally excluded by onlyExt. The rules file itself + the test file are in the rule's own exempt list.

### S5.7 — .claude/settings.json ships as managed path
The Claude Code harness hook travels with brain (like governance.yml). It's a NEW SESSION config — doesn't affect the current session. Already globally exempt from repo:check via BASE_GLOBAL_EXEMPT.

**Reshaped governance openspec to v2 floor+audit+golden-path model**

**What:** Reshaped all 4 governance openspec artifacts (proposal.md, design.md, spec.md, tasks.md) from the v1 "GitHub branch protection" model to the v2 "floor + additive hard gate + golden path" model.

**Why:** The v2 model (docs/inbox/workflow-governance-layer.md) is tool-agnostic and honest about the boundary: no tool-independent HARD guarantee exists on SaaS. The floor (hooks + audit) is universal; the platform gate is additive and conditional.

**Key architectural differences v1→v2:**
- v1 S4: memory-gate + decision-gate as CI YAML jobs (platform-conditional). REMOVED.
- v2 S4: generic checks library (scripts/governance/checks/) + full hook suite (commit-msg/pre-commit/pre-push) + brain:audit (re-verify merged history). Tool-independent.
- v2 S5 (NEW): self-gating golden-path verbs (brain:start/check/save/ship/next) + --no-verify policy (prohibited in repo:check + harness PreToolUse hook)
- v2 S3: protectBranch() now returns {enforced, reason, remedy} (never crashes on 403); capabilities() PROBED not hardcoded; brain:governance status added.
- GOVERNANCE_JOBS stays ['issue-link','diff-size'] — S4 does NOT add new CI jobs.

**Where:** openspec/changes/governance/{proposal.md, design.md, specs/governance/spec.md, tasks.md}. Engram topics sdd/governance/{proposal,design,spec,tasks} all updated.

**Learned:** The floor and hard gate COMPOSE — they don't fall back on each other. This distinction is load-bearing: client hooks are bypassable (soft, universal) while the platform gate is hard but conditional. brain:audit is the forge-proof universal teeth — verifies the outcome over merged history regardless of how the merge happened.

## Exploration: issue-97 — managed paths collision (scripts/ + .claude/settings.json)

### Current State

`brain/core/managed-paths.mjs` declares two colliding entries:
- `'scripts/**'` — brain claims the consumer's ROOT scripts/ directory and dumps ~87 files there on every upgrade
- `'.claude/settings.json'` — brain OVERWRITES the consumer's Claude Code permissions allowlist (plain copyFileSync in installer.mjs)

Synergy's `.claude/settings.json` is 4.7KB / 63 allow entries. Brain's `.claude/settings.json` is 15 lines / only the PreToolUse hook block. An upgrade would silently destroy the entire allowlist. Synergy's `.claude/settings.local.json` (another 200+ entries) is NOT in managed paths so it survives — but the consumer would lose the primary settings.json entirely.

Synergy currently has NO `scripts/` dir. If brain installed, 87 scripts would land there. If a consumer had `scripts/caso-uso-sesiones.sh`, it would survive (installer only copies, never deletes) but 87 more brain scripts would coexist — plus any shared filenames (e.g., `scripts/bootstrap.sh`) would be silently overwritten.

### Blast Radius — scripts/ → brain/scripts/ rename

**87 files to move** (git mv scripts/ brain/scripts/)

**Critical runtime references (break if not updated): ~74 across ~20 files**

Categories:
- **package.json script aliases**: 28 entries (`"node ./scripts/..."`, `"bash ./scripts/..."`, test glob)
- **bootstrap.sh**: 10 references incl. `git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks` (THE key coupling)
- **install-tools.sh**: 1 reference
- **day-start.mjs**: 4 references incl. `const HOOKS_PATH = 'scripts/hooks'` (self-heal mechanism)
- **hooks (pre-push, pre-commit, post-merge)**: 6 `node "$repo_root/scripts/..."` calls
- **brain-save.mjs**: 1 (`scripts/memory/cli.mjs`)
- **brain-next.mjs**: 1 (`scripts/check-refs.mjs`)
- **memory/lib/auto-resume.mjs**: 1 (`scripts/memory/cli.mjs`)
- **brain/core/managed-paths.mjs**: 1 (the `'scripts/**'` entry itself)
- **verify-change.mjs**: 2 (scope matcher logic: `f.startsWith('scripts/')`)
- **check-refs.mjs**: 1 (exempt list)
- **brain/project/check-refs-rules.mjs**: 2 (exempt list)
- **test container scripts** (fresh-install + upgrade in-container.sh): 8 references
- **test/fixtures/*/package.json** (4 files): 8 references (2 per fixture)

**Test assertions that would fail: ~15 across 6 test files**
- installer.test.mjs: 5 hardcoded `scripts/` fixture paths
- check-refs.test.mjs: 3 `addTrackedFile(git, dir, 'scripts/...')` fixtures  
- diff-size.test.mjs + diff-size-count.test.mjs: 4 numstat fixture strings
- i18n/coverage.test.mjs: 2 (hardcoded `scripts/hooks` in translation assertion)
- managed-paths.test.mjs: 1 implicit (tests managed array content)

**Doc/comment references: ~85 (non-breaking but should update)**
- README.md: 7 references (layer diagram, install commands, table)
- openspec design/tasks/spec docs: ~50
- docs/inbox: 3
- Source file header comments: ~25

**Self-hosting issue**: Brain's own repo IS the `scripts/` dir. The rename requires a coordinated atomic commit (`git mv` + all reference updates together) to avoid broken intermediate state. You CANNOT do this incrementally while the scripts themselves are running.

**Consumer migration concern**: Any existing consumer with brain installed has brain scripts at root `scripts/`. After the rename, `brain:upgrade` would copy to `brain/scripts/` but leave orphaned files at `scripts/`. A CHANGELOG + cleanup step is needed.

**core.hooksPath transition gap**: `core.hooksPath` is per-clone (not committed). After upgrade to renamed version, `day:start` checks `existsSync(HOOKS_PATH/pre-push)` where HOOKS_PATH would now be `brain/scripts/hooks`. If the file doesn't exist yet (first run after upgrade, before files copied), it WARNS and skips self-heal — one-time "no hooks" window. Acceptable but should be documented.

### Namespace Decision

Options considered:
- `brain/scripts/` — RECOMMENDED: completes the brain/ namespace (core + project + scripts). Natural. No dot-dir awkwardness.
- `brain/core/scripts/` — Wrong: brain/core is for methodology/docs, not executable scripts
- `.brain/` — Unusual hidden-dir pattern, same blast radius
- Keep `scripts/` — Zero blast but doesn't fix the collision

`brain/scripts/` is the right answer. It matches the existing structure conceptually.

NX friction: minimal. NX's `namedInputs.default` is `{projectRoot}/**/*` (per-project, not workspace root), so brain scripts in `brain/scripts/` at NX workspace root don't interfere with NX build targets. Root `package.json` brain aliases (`brain:upgrade`, `day:start`, etc.) coexist fine with NX scripts.

### settings.json Merge Design

**Today**: `copyFileSync(src, dest)` — pure overwrite in `installer.mjs:copyManaged()`

**New design** (additive merge, similar to `mergeDefaults` already in installer.mjs):
```js
function mergeClaudeSettings(existingPath, brainSettings) {
  // Fresh consumer (no existing file) → write brain's as-is
  if (!existsSync(existingPath)) return brainSettings;
  
  const existing = JSON.parse(readFileSync(existingPath, 'utf8'));
  const result = { ...existing };
  
  // Merge hooks.PreToolUse additively (deduplicate by command string)
  if (brainSettings.hooks?.PreToolUse) {
    result.hooks = result.hooks ?? {};
    result.hooks.PreToolUse = result.hooks.PreToolUse ?? [];
    for (const brainEntry of brainSettings.hooks.PreToolUse) {
      const alreadyPresent = result.hooks.PreToolUse.some(
        e => JSON.stringify(e) === JSON.stringify(brainEntry)
      );
      if (!alreadyPresent) result.hooks.PreToolUse.push(brainEntry);
    }
  }
  // Preserve all other consumer keys (permissions, other hooks, etc.)
  return result;
}
```

Wiring: in `brain-upgrade.mjs`, instead of letting `.claude/settings.json` go through `copyManaged` plain copy, handle it specially (either remove from managed array and apply merge post-copy, or add a `smartMerge` list to the installer).

`settings.local.json` — already safe: not in managed paths, never touched.

Fresh consumer: works — no existing file → write brain's 15-line hook block as-is.
Existing consumer: `permissions.allow` and all other keys preserved; only `hooks.PreToolUse` additively extended.

### Pre-upgrade Collision Guard Design

After implementing the settings.json merge, add a general backstop:

In `copyManaged()` (or `brain-upgrade.mjs`), before overwriting a file:
1. Read both the incoming brain file content and the consumer's existing file content
2. If they differ AND the consumer file exists → log a warning with the path and the diff summary
3. Two modes: `--dry-run` (existing, reports but doesn't write), new `--warn-collisions` (writes but warns)
4. Optionally: compare against PREVIOUS brain version's known content to detect "consumer modified a managed file" (the real bad case)

Simplest viable guard: detect when `destFile` exists and differs from `srcFile`, log all such cases before copying starts (pre-flight report), then proceed unless `--abort-on-collision` is set.

### Approaches Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Effort |
|----------|------|------|--------|
| Slice 1: settings.json merge only | Stops catastrophe NOW, zero blast | scripts/ collision remains | Low |
| Slice 1+2: merge + collision guard | Safe foundation for future install | Still no namespace fix | Low-Medium |
| Slice 3: full scripts/ rename | Eliminates collision structurally | 74 critical refs, 87 files mv, breaking | High |
| Do nothing | Nothing breaks | Consumers get burned on first upgrade | None |

### Recommended Slice Breakdown (ordered)

**Slice 1 — settings.json MERGE** (1 PR, ~150 lines)
- `scripts/lib/installer.mjs`: add `mergeClaudeSettings()` function
- `scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs`: call merge for `.claude/settings.json` instead of raw copy
- `brain/core/managed-paths.mjs`: either remove `.claude/settings.json` from `managed` (and handle separately) OR keep in managed and gate on merge in the upgrade script
- New unit test for `mergeClaudeSettings()`
- Stops the 4.7KB allowlist destruction immediately

**Slice 2 — Pre-upgrade collision guard** (1 PR, ~100 lines)
- `scripts/lib/installer.mjs`: add pre-flight collision detection to `copyManaged()`
- `scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs`: surface warnings prominently; add `--abort-on-collision` flag
- Unit tests for guard logic
- Provides backstop for ALL managed paths, not just settings.json

**Slice 3 — scripts/ → brain/scripts/ RENAME** (1 PR, MUST be atomic)
- `git mv scripts/ brain/scripts/` (87 files)
- Update 74 critical references across 20 files
- Update ~15 test assertions
- CHANGELOG entry (breaking change, migration guide for existing consumers)
- Update README install instructions
- This commit MUST be a single atomic commit — no intermediate state

**Slice 4 — Synergy validation** (investigation + docs, not a code change)
- Read-only: run `brain:upgrade --dry-run` on synergy after slices 1-3
- Document NX monorepo integration notes
- Verify the 3-layer README diagram still makes sense

### Risks

1. **Self-hosting atomicity**: Brain's scripts run during development of brain. The rename must be done in a single coordinated commit — cannot rename incrementally while scripts are live. Risk: if the git mv + all references don't happen together, brain's own workflows break mid-rename.

2. **Existing consumer breaking change**: Any consumer that added brain's npm script aliases to their package.json pointing at `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` etc. must update those after upgrading to the renamed version. This is a hard breaking change requiring a migration guide in CHANGELOG.

3. **`core.hooksPath` one-time gap**: After upgrade, `core.hooksPath` still points to old `scripts/hooks`. The `day:start` self-heal checks `existsSync(brain/scripts/hooks/pre-push)` and finds it present (upgrade already copied files), then reconfigures. But ONLY if `brain:upgrade` ran BEFORE `day:start`. Order matters: `brain:upgrade` → `day:start` (or `env:init`).

4. **NX build cache pollution**: brain scripts landing at workspace root are not in any NX project's `projectRoot` so they don't affect per-project caching. Minor concern: NX affected detection might include `brain/scripts/**` in workspace-level changes, but this is benign.

5. **`node_modules/brain/brain/scripts/` path for initial bootstrap**: The README currently tells consumers to run `node node_modules/brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs`. After rename it becomes `node node_modules/brain/brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs`. The `brain/brain/` repetition looks odd but is technically correct. The test fixtures and container tests hardcode this path — all must be updated.

### Affected Files Summary

Critical path files:
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/brain/core/managed-paths.mjs` — managed list (both problems root here)
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs` — copyManaged (plain overwrite, needs merge)
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs` — orchestrates copy
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/day-start.mjs` — HOOKS_PATH constant + 3 spawn calls
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/bootstrap.sh` — core.hooksPath + 9 node calls
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/hooks/pre-push` — 4 node calls to scripts/
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/hooks/pre-commit` — 1 node call
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/scripts/hooks/post-merge` — 1 node call
- `/home/gandalf/IA/brain/.claude/settings.json` — 15-line hook block (what brain distributes)
- `/home/gandalf/IA/synergy/.claude/settings.json` — 4.7KB, 63 allow entries (what would be overwritten)

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — blast radius is fully mapped, both fixes are designed, slice ordering is clear.

## Proposal — Managed-Paths Namespace & Merge Safety (issue #97)

**Status:** Proposed. Artifact store HYBRID. File: openspec/changes/managed-paths-namespace/proposal.md

### Problem (two collisions, one root cause)
brain copies managed paths into a consumer on `brain:upgrade`. The list was authored against brain's own repo (all paths brain-owned); Docker install tests install into an EMPTY container so nothing ever collides — tests are green because the env has nothing to collide with. A real install into NX monorepo /home/gandalf/IA/synergy exposed two collisions:
- **A — `.claude/settings.json` OVERWRITTEN (catastrophic):** installer.mjs:copyManaged() does plain copyFileSync. brain's settings.json = 15 lines (only hooks.PreToolUse). synergy's = 4.7KB / 63 permissions.allow entries → silently destroyed. (settings.local.json survives — not managed.)
- **B — `scripts/**` claims consumer ROOT scripts/:** brain dumps 87 files into consumer's scripts/; shared filenames overwritten. Consumer's scripts/ no longer theirs.

Root cause: brain treats two consumer-owned surfaces as managed.

### Settled decisions
1. Namespace to **`brain/scripts/`** — completes 3-pillar model (brain/core managed methodology, brain/project consumer-owned, brain/scripts managed harness). Rejected `.brain/` (same blast, no benefit) and keep-scripts/ (no fix).
2. **MERGE settings.json** via `mergeClaudeSettings()` — additively insert brain's hooks.PreToolUse, deduped by serialized entry, preserve permissions.allow + other keys. Fresh consumer → brain's block as-is. settings.local.json untouched.
3. **Pre-upgrade collision guard** in copyManaged() + `--abort-on-collision` flag — general backstop so next undiscovered collision fails loud.

### 4 slices (chained PRs, feature-branch-chain, tracker feature/issue-97-managed-paths) — highest-value-first
- **S1 — settings.json MERGE (~150 lines):** STOPS DATA LOSS NOW. mergeClaudeSettings() in installer.mjs, wire in brain-upgrade.mjs, gate .claude/settings.json out of raw copy, tests (fixture w/ 63-entry allowlist proves no clobber). Independently shippable.
- **S2 — collision guard (~100 lines):** pre-flight diff check in copyManaged() + --abort-on-collision, tests.
- **S3 — scripts/ → brain/scripts/ ATOMIC rename:** git mv 87 files + ~74 critical refs across ~20 files (28 package.json aliases, bootstrap.sh core.hooksPath, day-start.mjs HOOKS_PATH, hooks, verbs, managed-paths.mjs, verify-change.mjs scope matcher, check-refs exempt lists, test-container scripts, 4 fixtures) + ~15 test assertions + README/CHANGELOG. MUST be SINGLE ATOMIC COMMIT (brain runs its own scripts; half-renamed state breaks brain). BREAKING.
- **S4 — synergy validation (docs/dry-run):** brain:upgrade --dry-run on synergy = zero collisions; NX integration notes; verify README 3-pillar diagram.

### Breaking change & migration (S3)
- Existing consumers keep orphaned root scripts/ after upgrade → installer never deletes; CHANGELOG MUST say "delete scripts/ after upgrading to vX.Y.Z".
- Alias path becomes node_modules/brain/brain/scripts/... (double brain/, intentional).
- Warrants minor/major bump — number deferred to release.
- **core.hooksPath one-time window:** per-clone, not committed. After upgrade but before next env:init/day:start, hooks point at stale scripts/hooks → self-heals on next day:start. Required order: brain:upgrade → day:start/env:init. Document in upgrade notes.

### Out of scope
Deeper NX integration beyond dry-run (follow-up); .brain/ alternate; auto-delete orphaned scripts/; touching settings.local.json; other managed paths.

### Rollback
S1 additive, revert function+wiring. S2 read-only+opt-in flag. S3 revert single atomic commit (clean, no half-state). S4 docs only.

### ADR note
Alters managed-paths model + establishes merge-don't-overwrite rule → likely **ADR-0006 update** (or new ADR) covering the 3-pillar core/project/scripts split + merge-vs-overwrite policy. Author alongside S3. This proposal flags it, does not author it.

### Risks / open questions
- Self-hosting atomicity of S3 (the dominant risk).
- Exact version number (deferred).
- core.hooksPath transition gap (documented, acceptable).

**next_recommended:** sdd-spec + sdd-design (parallel).

# Design: Managed-Paths Namespace & Merge Safety (issue #97)

HYBRID artifact. File: openspec/changes/managed-paths-namespace/design.md

## Technical Approach
Two consumer-owned surfaces wrongly `managed` and clobbered on brain:upgrade: `.claude/settings.json` (plain copyFileSync overwrite) + root `scripts/**`. Three composable mechanisms across 4 chained PRs (feature-branch-chain, tracker feature/issue-97-managed-paths): S1 merge settings.json, S2 collision guard, S3 atomic scripts/→brain/scripts/ rename, S4 synergy dry-run docs. Merge and guard composable: settings.json takes merge path, EXCLUDED from collision guard.

## Decisions
1. **specialMerge map in installer API (RECOMMENDED over alternatives)**: copyManaged() gains `specialMerge: {relPath → mergeFn}`. .claude/settings.json STAYS in managed (still distributed + drift-checked) but routes through mergeClaudeSettings instead of copyFileSync. Keeps copy/skip/merge policy in ONE unit-testable place, mirrors mergeDefaults/migrateConfig seam, generalizes. Rejected: (a) remove from managed + bespoke post-copy merge in brain-upgrade.mjs (scatters policy, breaks drift guard); (b) raw copy (the bug). dry-run reports `merged` distinct from `copied`.
2. **mergeClaudeSettings(existingPath, brainSettingsPath) mirrors mergeDefaults**: fresh consumer (no dest)→write brain's as-is; existing→spread consumer obj, additively append brain's hooks.PreToolUse deduped by JSON.stringify, preserve permissions.allow + all other keys. brain only OWNS PreToolUse block (ADR-0014 §9). Existing-value-wins invariant. Idempotent.
3. **Collision guard**: in copyManaged(), pre-write, for each managed file NOT a specialMerge target: dest exists AND bytes differ from src → collect. Return collisions[]. brain:upgrade surfaces report; --abort-on-collision throws BEFORE any write (all-or-nothing, clean rollback). Default: warn+proceed (current behavior). settings.json excluded (uses merge).
4. **S3 ONE atomic commit**: git mv scripts/→brain/scripts/ (87 files) + all refs + test assertions in SINGLE commit. Order: git mv → rewrite refs → run suite + real dry-run → commit. WHY: self-hosting — brain runs its own scripts/ (hooks, day:start, governance workflow); half-renamed state breaks brain's own tooling (core.hooksPath, aliases, inter-script calls). Revert = one clean commit.
5. **core.hooksPath transition**: NOT migrated by installer (per-clone, not committed). Documented order brain:upgrade→day:start/env:init. day:start self-heals once HOOKS_PATH constant = brain/scripts/hooks. One-time stale window acceptable, documented.

## S3 Reference MAP (~74 refs / ~20 files)

**sdd/issue-97-managed-paths/spec**

# Managed-Paths Namespace & Merge Safety Specification

## Purpose

Eliminates two silent data-loss collisions in `brain:upgrade` — settings.json overwrite
and scripts/ namespace takeover — by introducing a merge strategy for shared consumer
config, a general pre-upgrade collision guard, and a `brain/scripts/` namespace for the
managed harness. The change completes brain's 3-pillar model: `brain/core` (managed
methodology), `brain/project` (consumer-owned overrides), `brain/scripts` (managed harness
verbs). The consumer's root `scripts/` is restored to consumer ownership.

## Epic Invariant

`brain:upgrade` MUST NOT overwrite consumer-owned content. Every path in the `managed`
array MUST be either (a) exclusively brain-owned, or (b) merged additively so consumer
keys are preserved and provably intact after every upgrade.

## Requirement Index

| Req | Slice | Name | Testable |
|-----|-------|------|---------|
| REQ-S1-1 | 1 | mergeClaudeSettings — fresh consumer | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S1-2 | 1 | mergeClaudeSettings — existing consumer, no clobber | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S1-3 | 1 | mergeClaudeSettings — idempotent re-run | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S1-4 | 1 | settings.local.json never touched | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S1-5 | 1 | .claude/settings.json excluded from raw copyManaged | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S2-1 | 2 | Pre-flight collision report | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S2-2 | 2 | --abort-on-collision aborts before any write | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S2-3 | 2 | No false positive when dest is identical or absent | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S3-1 | 3 | managed-paths declares brain/scripts/**, not scripts/** | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S3-2 | 3 | All runtime references resolve under brain/scripts/ | Full suite + integration |
| REQ-S3-3 | 3 | Consumer root scripts/ is not a managed path | Unit (`node --test`) |
| REQ-S3-4 | 3 | CHANGELOG documents breaking change and migration | File assertion |
| REQ-S3-5 | 3 | core.hooksPath transition window documented | File assertion |
| REQ-S3-6 | 3 | Single atomic commit delivers the rename | Git history assertion |
| REQ-S4-1 | 4 | brain:upgrade --dry-run on synergy: zero collisions | Manual / dry-run |
| REQ-E-1 | epic | brain:upgrade never overwrites consumer-owned content | Verified by S1+S2+S3 |

---

## Slice 1 — `.claude/settings.json` MERGE

### REQ-S1-1: Fresh consumer

#### Scenario: No existing settings.json — brain block written
- GIVEN no `.claude/settings.json` exists in the consumer repo
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs (via `mergeClaudeSettings()`)
- THEN the consumer's `.claude/settings.json` is created with brain's `hooks.PreToolUse` block
- AND its content is byte-for-byte identical to brain's 15-line settings block

### REQ-S1-2: Existing consumer, no clobber

#### Scenario: 63-entry permissions.allow survives upgrade
- GIVEN a consumer `.claude/settings.json` with 63 `permissions.allow` entries
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs
- THEN the result file contains all 63 original `permissions.allow` entries
- AND brain's `hooks.PreToolUse` entries are present
- AND no consumer key is absent from the merged result

#### Scenario: Consumer hooks not owned by brain are preserved
- GIVEN a consumer `.claude/settings.json` with a custom `hooks.PreToolUse` entry not in brain's block
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs
- THEN the custom entry is still present alongside brain's entries

### REQ-S1-3: Idempotent

#### Scenario: Second upgrade adds nothing
- GIVEN `brain:upgrade` has already merged brain's `hooks.PreToolUse` into the consumer
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs a second time
- THEN the `.claude/settings.json` is byte-for-byte identical to the post-first-run result
- AND no brain `hooks.PreToolUse` entry appears more than once

### REQ-S1-4: settings.local.json never touched

#### Scenario: settings.local.json is byte-identical before and after upgrade
- GIVEN a consumer `settings.local.json` with arbitrary content
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs
- THEN `settings.local.json` is byte-for-byte identical to its pre-upgrade state

### REQ-S1-5: .claude/settings.json excluded from raw copyManaged

#### Scenario: Raw copyManaged never writes settings.json
- GIVEN a consumer with an existing `.claude/settings.json`
- WHEN `copyManaged()` iterates managed paths
- THEN `.claude/settings.json` is NOT written via `copyFileSync` at any point during the run

---

## Slice 2 — Pre-Upgrade Collision Guard

### REQ-S2-1: Pre-flight collision report

#### Scenario: Differing managed file produces collision record
- GIVEN a managed path whose destination exists with content different from the incoming brain file
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs the pre-flight check
- THEN the collision is recorded AND the report is printed before any file is written

#### Scenario: Collision report printed before first write
- GIVEN two managed paths have collisions
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs
- THEN both collision paths appear in the pre-flight output before no managed file is overwritten

### REQ-S2-2: --abort-on-collision

#### Scenario: --abort-on-collision aborts before any write
- GIVEN a managed path whose destination differs from brain's version
- WHEN `brain:upgrade --abort-on-collision` runs
- THEN the command exits non-zero AND no managed file is written to disk

#### Scenario: No collision — proceeds normally
- GIVEN all managed path destinations are absent or identical to brain's versions
- WHEN `brain:upgrade --abort-on-collision` runs
- THEN the command exits zero and writes proceed normally

### REQ-S2-3: No false positive

#### Scenario: Absent destination is not a collision
- GIVEN a managed path whose destination does not exist
- WHEN the pre-flight check runs
- THEN no collision is recorded for that path

#### Scenario: Identical destination is not a collision
- GIVEN a managed path whose destination is byte-for-byte identical to the brain source
- WHEN the pre-flight check runs
- THEN no collision is recorded for that path

---

## Slice 3 — `scripts/` → `brain/scripts/` Atomic Rename (BREAKING)

### REQ-S3-1: managed-paths declares brain/scripts/**

#### Scenario: managed array contains brain/scripts/**
- GIVEN S3 has merged
- WHEN the `managed` export from `managed-paths.mjs` is inspected
- THEN `'brain/scripts/**'` is present AND `'scripts/**'` is absent

### REQ-S3-2: All runtime references resolve under brain/scripts/

#### Scenario: npm test green after rename
- GIVEN S3 has merged as a single atomic commit
- WHEN `npm test` runs in the brain repo
- THEN all tests exit zero

#### Scenario: hooks, verbs, and bootstrap resolve correctly
- GIVEN `bootstrap.sh` and `day-start.mjs` have been updated
- WHEN `core.hooksPath` is inspected after a fresh `env:init`
- THEN it resolves to `brain/scripts/hooks`

#### Scenario: Fresh-install integration test passes
- GIVEN a clean Docker test container
- WHEN the fresh-install integration test runs
- THEN the install succeeds with no broken path references

#### Scenario: Upgrade integration test passes
- GIVEN a Docker test container with a previous brain installation
- WHEN the upgrade integration test runs
- THEN `brain:upgrade` completes with all files under `brain/scripts/`

### REQ-S3-3: Consumer root scripts/ is not a managed path

#### Scenario: Consumer file under root scripts/ survives upgrade
- GIVEN a consumer with a file at `scripts/consumer-sentinel.sh`
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs after S3 merges
- THEN `scripts/consumer-sentinel.sh` is byte-for-byte identical to its pre-upgrade state
- AND no brain file is written under root `scripts/`

### REQ-S3-4: CHANGELOG documents breaking change

#### Scenario: CHANGELOG contains orphaned-scripts cleanup instruction
- GIVEN S3 has merged
- WHEN `CHANGELOG.md` is read
- THEN it contains an instruction to delete root `scripts/` after upgrading
- AND it references the new bootstrap path `node_modules/brain/brain/scripts/`
- AND it specifies the `brain:upgrade` → `day:start`/`env:init` required order

### REQ-S3-5: core.hooksPath transition window documented

#### Scenario: core.hooksPath transition gap is documented
- GIVEN S3 has merged
- WHEN the CHANGELOG or upgrade notes are read
- THEN the text explains that `core.hooksPath` points to the old path until `day:start` self-heals
- AND the mitigation order (`brain:upgrade` then `day:start`) is explicitly stated

### REQ-S3-6: Single atomic commit

#### Scenario: One commit contains move and all reference updates
- GIVEN S3 has merged
- WHEN `git show <S3-commit-sha> --stat` is run
- THEN both moved `brain/scripts/` files and updated references appear in the same commit
- AND no prior commit in the S3 branch contains a partial rename

---

## Slice 4 — Synergy Validation

### REQ-S4-1: brain:upgrade --dry-run on synergy reports zero collisions

#### Scenario: Dry-run on synergy reports zero collisions
- GIVEN S1, S2, and S3 have merged
- WHEN `brain:upgrade --dry-run` is run targeting `/home/gandalf/IA/synergy`
- THEN the output contains zero collision records AND the command exits zero

#### Scenario: NX integration notes written
- GIVEN S4 is complete
- WHEN the brain docs are inspected
- THEN NX integration notes exist covering workspace-root coexistence, `namedInputs` non-interference, and root `package.json` alias coexistence

---

## Epic Requirements

### REQ-E-1: brain:upgrade MUST NOT Overwrite Consumer-Owned Content

#### Scenario: Upgrade on synergy consumer produces no data loss
- GIVEN synergy with its 63-entry `permissions.allow` and no root `scripts/` dir
- WHEN `brain:upgrade` runs after S1–S3 merge
- THEN `synergy/.claude/settings.json` retains all 63 `permissions.allow` entries
- AND brain's `hooks.PreToolUse` block is present
- AND no file under synergy's workspace is unexpectedly overwritten

---

## Gaps and Assumptions

| # | Gap / Assumption |
|---|-----------------|
| G1 | Integration tests (REQ-S3-2) require Docker or equivalent isolated environment; not coverable by `node --test` alone. |
| G2 | Version bump number for S3 breaking change deferred to release time. |
| G3 | S4 dry-run is manual acceptance, not automated. |
| G4 | Orphaned root scripts/ cleanup is a documented manual step; brain:upgrade MUST NOT auto-delete consumer files. |
| G5 | ADR update (ADR-0006 or new ADR) covering 3-pillar model and merge-vs-overwrite policy is flagged by proposal and deferred to S3 authorship. |
