## 4. Implicit canonical contract as coded today + cross-gate inconsistencies (B0 must resolve)
Implicit contract (inferred from gate code): dir `openspec/changes/issue-<N>[-<slug>]/` (slug optional per new-change.mjs, though the doc/workflow-guide.md always shows it present), containing proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md always, and a spec artifact under EITHER `spec.md` OR `specs/*/spec.md` (phase-order-check.mjs is the only gate that tolerates both — check-refs.mjs and new-change.mjs only know about proposal.md/tasks.md and don't check/produce spec.md at all). Checked-task pattern `- [x]` (case-insensitive, phase-order-check.mjs only). Status frontmatter ladder (8 values, phase-order-check.mjs only — no other gate reads `status:`). `archive` is a reserved/excluded dir name in 3 places (check-refs, session-start, feature-resolution) but no gate defines where archived changes actually live (no `openspec/changes/archive/<iid>/` literal found anywhere — Track E1 in the PLAN says this move doesn't exist yet, confirmed: `brain:change:archive` verb is listed as NOT YET BUILT, depends on B1). `resume.md` lives at `openspec/changes/<feature>/resume.md` (engram.mjs, feature-resolution.mjs) — used as a disambiguation signal for "which change is actively worked," not documented as a required artifact anywhere in harness-contract.md's artifact contract table.

Inconsistencies B0 must decide/resolve:
1. spec.md is documented as required (harness-contract.md, workflow-guide.md) but NOT created by the scaffolder (new-change.mjs) and NOT checked by check-refs.mjs S-1 — only phase-order-check.mjs (a DETECTION_JOBS, non-blocking-by-default gate) even looks for it, and it accepts two shapes.
2. new-change.mjs's changeId omits the slug when --title is absent, producing `issue-<N>/` instead of `issue-<N>-<slug>/` — diverges from the canonical pattern documented in harness-contract.md:50 and workflow-guide.md:73-76.
3. Two independent "is this change done" vocabularies exist with no cross-check: STATUS_LADDER frontmatter values in phase-order-check.mjs vs. checked-task-count in the same file vs. resume.md frontmatter fields (resume-schema.mjs, not yet inventoried in depth here).
4. No gate/script defines the archive destination path as a literal — Track E1 (archive verb) is unbuilt; B1's accessor should decide this path now rather than let E1 invent a second one later.

## 5. Manual/B2 `plain` grounding — what a human does by hand today
docs/workflow-guide.md:46-99, section "B. Manual (no AI — npm verbs in sequence)":
1. `npm run brain:env:init` (one-time)
2. `npm run brain:session:start` (session open)
3. `npm run brain:ticket:start -- <id>` (branch creation)
4. `npm run brain:project:feature -- --issue <id>` — "scaffolds the artifact folder" (comment at workflow-guide.md:69) — but per §3 above, new-change.mjs only actually writes proposal.md/design.md/tasks.md, NOT spec.md, contradicting workflow-guide.md:74 which lists spec.md as one of the 4 files to "edit by hand, in order."
5. Manual edit of all 4 artifacts (guide claims 4, tool delivers 3)
6. Manual code implementation, checking off tasks.md items by hand
7. `npm run brain:repo:check` + `npm test` + `npm run brain:change:verify` (gates)
8. `npm run memory:share` (memory-gate)
9. Commit + PR with "Closes #<id>"
This IS effectively today's de-facto "plain" backend already — it's just not packaged as a `harness/backends/plain.mjs` module; it's the golden-path npm verbs used directly, all harness-neutral already (new-change.mjs, verify-change.mjs, check-refs.mjs are unconditional, not gated by SDD_HARNESS). B2's real incremental work is therefore narrower than "implement the full verb set" — most verbs already work standalone; B2 mainly needs to (a) fix the proposal/design/tasks-only scaffold to also emit spec.md (closing gap #1 above), and (b) decide whether `plain` as a harness/backends module should just be a thin manifest declaring "these already-neutral scripts are my implementation" versus genuinely new code.

Only 6 real sites exist across 5 files: check-refs.mjs, session-start.mjs, phase-order-check.mjs, new-change.mjs, engram.mjs (x2), feature-resolution.mjs.

**FINDING (C4 review MAJOR-1, needs ruling): records-only pull re-stamps created_at — engram save has no timestamp flag, local recency ordering skewed after every pull**

What: Fresh-review MAJOR-1 on C4 (#229). The records-only pull (D2) writes each observation via `engram save`, which accepts --type/--project/--scope/--topic but has NO timestamp flag. So `importRecord()` computes `created_at: toEngramNaive(record.ts)` but the save primitive DISCARDS it — every hydrated observation is re-stamped with engram's wall-clock insert time. The OLD `engram sync --import` (chunk transport) preserved original timestamps; the records-only path does not.

Impact: recency-ordered LOCAL engram search/mem_context is skewed after every pull (all hydrated obs get ~now). NOT data loss: the committed `.memory/records/` keeps the correct `ts` (source of truth); engram is a rebuildable cache. Does NOT affect idempotency (topic_key upsert keys on project+scope+topic, all stable).

Status: DISCLOSED in code (comment at _defaultEngramSave, engram.mjs ~985) + MINOR-1 fixed in same pass (now passes --scope so importRecord's declared scope is honored). NEEDS HUMAN RULING at CP-C4: (a) ACCEPT as documented + file follow-up to add engram-side timestamp-preserving ingestion (a --created-at flag or a bulk records-import verb) — recommended, since records/ is source of truth and the fix is engram-side (out of C4 scope); or (b) block C4 until timestamps can be preserved.

Where: brain/scripts/memory/backends/engram.mjs (_defaultEngramSave + importMemory call site), importRecord (engram-import.mjs:71 computes created_at). Related: [[sdd/issue-229-c4/kickoff]]. content:
**FINDING #12 (CP-A2b live): gitlab.mjs issueView hardcodes glab CLI → crashes in node:20 CI image → issue-link fail-closed; fixtures inject fetchIssue so never caught it**

What: CP-A2b ran LIVE on the gitlab.com mirror. Validated: all 8 jobs ran (include: resolved), actor-check warn+pass (Amendment 3 confirmed), MR-A (no issue link) BLOCKED at rung 1. BUT MR-B failed `issue-link`: the REQUIRED gate's `defaultFetchIssue` → `getVcs().issueView` → `gitlab.mjs` runs `glab api`, and the CI image (node:20) has NO `glab` binary → the spawn crashes → fail-closed (correct DIRECTION, but the trigger is infrastructure, not a real governance failure).

Why the fixtures missed it: every run-check/issue-link test INJECTS `fetchIssue` (dependency injection for hermeticity), so no test ever EXECUTES the real provider binary. The seam's injectability — the same property that makes tests hermetic (finding #10) — HID a real image dependency. Testing lesson: an injectable-seam suite proves the LOGIC but not that the DEFAULT implementation runs in the target environment; a CI-consumed verb needs a test asserting it spawns no external CLI (or an env-level smoke).

DESIGN DECISION (drafted; reviewer rules): (a) install glab per job (before_script) — REJECTED-lean: an image dependency in EVERY consumer, and an include: that demands a CLI install weakens ADR-0018's portability (the core argument). (b) rewrite the CI-consumed GitLab provider verbs over DIRECT API v4 fetch with VCS_TOKEN — reviewer's lean, and MINE: zero image deps, coherent with the repo's zero-dep policy, glab stays for local interactive. PRECEDENT EXISTS IN-REPO: ci-context.mjs `defaultFetchMr` (loadGitlabContext) already fetches direct API v4 (CI_API_V4_URL ?? gitlab.com/api/v4, PRIVATE-TOKEN header, ProxyAgent(HTTPS_PROXY)). issueView is a simple GET `/projects/:encoded/issues/:iid` → mirror that helper (factor it shared). Cost: LOW.

Doctrine this sets: CI-consumed provider verbs must be CLI-FREE (direct API). Extends to actor-check's `gh`-hardcoded fetchLabeledEvents (m3) — same class, A3 territory.

PENDING (do NOT start until the log): local-checks ALSO failed on both MRs — suspicion: a seam test coupled to real git + the runner's shallow clone (candidate: the A1 `git diff HEAD...HEAD` ci-context test). Awaiting the log before any fix.

Where: brain/scripts/vcs/providers/gitlab.mjs issueView (glab), brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context.mjs defaultFetchMr (the direct-fetch template), brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs defaultFetchIssue. Related: [[sdd/issue-231-a2/done]], [[findings/github-issuelink-bash-hardcoded-main]].

content:
**FINDING #10 + doctrine candidate: gate tests with default readers over the real repo = verdicts coupled to committed state**

What: Finding #10 — a hermeticity bug in the tests shipped in PR #227 (run-check.test.mjs). Two memory-gate tests that expect FAIL injected `readChunks` but NOT `readRecords`, so the runner's default `readRecords` read the REAL `.memory/records/`. On the tracker (no records/) they passed; on the cutover branch (33 session_summaries in records/) the gate wrongly PASSES and the fail-expecting test FAILS. A test whose verdict depends on committed memory state.

Reproduced hermetically (no real-store mutation): runCheck('memory-gate', {cwd: <dir with records/session_summary>, readChunks: () => [{type:'decision'}]}) → {pass:true} (wrong); same with a records-less cwd → {pass:false} (correct).

The two active bugs: "injected chunks have no session_summary → fail" and "main: memory-gate failing → returns 1". Audit found 3 more latent violations (tests injecting only readChunks that happened to still pass). Fix: all 5 memory-gate tests now inject BOTH readChunks AND readRecords (readRecords: () => [] where records must be empty). Verified: run the test file from a cwd WITH records/ present → all 7 memory-gate subtests pass. Full suite 1049 pass.

Sibling observation (NOT fixed, intentional): the decision-gate ci-context-seam test (run-check.test.mjs, "deps.ctx.baseSha/headSha take precedence...") runs real `git diff HEAD...HEAD` via the default diffNameOnly path — it deliberately exercises real git as the thing under test (passes in-repo). Different class from the accidental-default memory bug.

DOCTRINE CANDIDATE (human ruling, register in catalog or testing doctrine): runCheck gate tests MUST inject ALL evidence sources; never inherit a default that reads the real world (real .memory/ or real git). Rule of thumb encoded in the file header comment: "whoever injects one gate reader injects both." Generalization: any pure-check runner test that leaves an I/O dep at its default couples the verdict to ambient repo state.

Where: brain/scripts/governance/run-check.test.mjs (header comment + 5 memory-gate tests). Related: [[governance/memory-gate-records-aware]] (PR #227, where the bug shipped), unblocks cutover #225.

**The doctrine (binding):** `brain/core/**` methodology docs + `brain/HOME.md` + `brain/core/templates/HOME.template.md` are DOC zone. ### Designed Empirical-Experiment Batch (Pin 3 — hand to human operating real Antigravity)

> Format: EXPERIMENT / RUN / CAPTURE, each with a mandatory `Antigravity version:` field. Do not assume answers — these must be measured.

**Experiment 1 — Which instruction file(s) does Antigravity load, and what precedence?**
- `Antigravity version: ____________`
- EXPERIMENT: Determine which candidate instruction file Antigravity actually reads when multiple exist, and its load precedence.
- RUN:
  1. In a scratch/test repo (not `brain` itself), create three candidate files with a UNIQUE sentinel string in each:
     - `AGENTS.md` containing the line `SENTINEL-AGENTS-7f3a: if you can see this, you loaded AGENTS.md`
     - `CLAUDE.md` containing the line `SENTINEL-CLAUDE-9b2c: if you can see this, you loaded CLAUDE.md`
     - Antigravity's own native config file, if one is documented (e.g. `.antigravity/config` or similar — check Antigravity's own docs for the exact native path first; if none is documented, skip this third candidate and note "no native config format found" instead of guessing) containing `SENTINEL-NATIVE-1e5d: if you can see this, you loaded the native config`
  2. Open Antigravity in that scratch repo.
  3. Prompt EXACTLY: `"List every sentinel string (format SENTINEL-*) you can currently see in your loaded context, and name the exact file each one came from."`

In the scratch repo (with `.memory/records/` seeded per brain's format — copy a real record shape from `.memory/records/2026-07.jsonl`), prompt Antigravity with EXACTLY: `"Remember this fact for future sessions in this project: the sentinel value is MEMORY-PROBE-4d8f. **What**: Before applying `status:approved` to an old issue, re-measure its factual claims (site counts, file lists, consumer inventories) against the current base branch. An issue's count is a measurement like any other — point-in-time, and stale by approval time.

**Why**: The #247 scope-check (before the B2 Antigravity baptism) found the issue's "3 chunk-consumer sites" was wrong when re-measured against origin/feature/v2.0.0: it was actually **2 code sites** (`brain-audit.mjs`, `brain-check.mjs`, both via `readChunkObservations`) + **2 transitive invokers** of brain-audit (`release.yml:43`, `governance-postmerge.yml:42` — both run `node brain-audit.mjs`, zero readChunkObservations of their own). The original table even mis-paired `release.yml` with brain-check (release.yml invokes brain-audit). Owner ruling: correct the body before approve; the reviewer independently confirmed 2+2.

**How to apply**:
1. `git grep -n <symbol> origin/<base>` for the real consumers; separate CODE sites from TRANSITIVE invokers (a workflow that runs a script ≠ a code site). Name transitive coverage EXPLICITLY in the issue so the implementer does not hunt for a symbol that isn't there.
2. Watch for orphans: if a migration removes the last consumer of a module (e.g. `chunk-reader.mjs`), the slice must carry a retirement verdict (deprecate vs delete) — don't leave a dead reader unruled.
3. Watch for scope bleed in the acceptance criteria: verification evidence that belongs to another track (e.g. pre-receive push-rejection = CP-A4a, not the chunk migration) must be struck.

**Where**: GitHub #247 (body corrected 2026-07-12); base origin/feature/v2.0.0. Related: [[doctrine-mechanical-gates-catch-what-review-cannot]] — same family (measured-not-declared).

**Learned**: A stale issue count reads as authoritative because it's written down, exactly the trap the "mechanical gates catch what review can't see" doctrine warns about — the fix is to re-run the measurement, not to trust the prose.

This is stricter than Claude Code's prefix-based `command(git commit:*)` style. Related: [[sdd/issue-256-b2/baptism-complete]].

**Worktree workspace model MEASURED: ticket-start --worktree works in v2, engram unifies across worktrees (git_remote), adopt for parallel team**

**What**: Decision to adopt `brain:ticket:start --worktree --base feature/v2.0.0` as the workspace model for the heterogeneous parallel team (Claude Code on D2, Antigravity on E1), replacing separate clones. Grounded in three measurements (owner asked to measure before proposing).

**Why**: The owner proposed worktrees-per-task (which brain 0.x supported) as the scale model vs n separate clones. Measured, it wins: cheap (shared object store, single fetch, zero-dep), natural one-branch-per-worktree lock.

**The 3 measurements**:
1. `ticket-start.mjs:138-207` STILL creates worktrees in v2 — the 0.x machinery was NOT retired. Wired as `brain:ticket:start`; `--worktree` does `git worktree add <parent>/<repo>-issue-<id> -b <branch> <base>`, supports `--base <branch>`, copies `.env` (not inherited by worktrees), runs feature-resume inside. So it's ADOPTED, not a revival micro-slice.
2. **engram does NOT fragment memory across worktrees.** Probed with a throwaway worktree: `git remote get-url origin` from the worktree = the identical origin URL as main (`https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain.git`). engram resolves project by `git_remote` (every mem_save this session reported `project_source: git_remote`), so a worktree = the SAME project "brain". The finding-#8 concern ("a worktree is another project by path") does NOT apply to git_remote resolution. The worktree's `.git` is `gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>` — one shared object store, single fetch.
3. Antigravity's `trustedWorkspaces[]` auto-adds each new dir on trust, so each new worktree needs one operator "trust" action — a known minor operational step. Cleanup: strip scratch/worktree entries on teardown.

**Bonus**: `brain:ticket:start --worktree --base feature/v2.0.0` would have PREVENTED baptism finding #2 (Antigravity's PR was born pointing at `main` because the base was set manually) — the tool sets the base explicitly. Adopting worktrees removes an already-observed error class, not just adds scale.

**Where**: `brain/scripts/ticket-start.mjs`, `package.json` (`brain:ticket:start`). Base for all parallel work: `feature/v2.0.0`.

**Learned**: engram's project identity is the git remote, not the filesystem path — so any same-repo worktree/clone with the same origin shares one memory project. This is the mechanism that makes worktrees safe for the parallel team. Related: [[architecture/worktree-workspace-model]], [[reference/antigravity-cli-settings]], [[sdd/issue-256-b2/baptism-complete]].

**What**: Definitive measurement of whether an engram memory-save from a sibling git worktree scopes to a phantom project (finding-#8 territory). ANSWER: NO — a worktree with an `origin` remote resolves to the same project as the main repo (`brain`).

**The measurement (engram's own logic)**: `detect_project()` in `~/.claude/plugins/cache/engram/engram/0.1.1/scripts/_helpers.sh:7-33` is a LADDER:
1. `git -C "$dir" remote get-url origin` → repo name from URL. This is a GIT COMMAND, worktree-safe (a worktree's `.git` is a file `gitdir:` pointer, but `git -C <worktree>` resolves through it). Ran it against the worktree: origin = `https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain.git` → derived name `brain`. Sourced the real helper: `detect_project(/home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-259)` = `brain`.
2. Fallback `git -C "$dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel` → basename — THIS would give `brain-issue-259` (phantom), BUT is only reached if step 1 fails. Origin resolves in our worktree, so step 2 is never reached.
3. Final fallback `basename "$dir"`.
The MCP resolution ladder (DOCS.md) matches: level 2 `git_remote` (cwd is a git root with origin) → repo name from remote URL. `mem_current_project` live = `{project: brain, project_source: git_remote}`.

**The two documented (non-improvised) safeguards** if ever running a save with the MCP process cwd = worktree AND origin somehow absent: (a) `ENGRAM_PROJECT=brain` env var — process-level default, takes precedence over cwd detection for the MCP lifetime; (b) explicit `project: 'brain'` on `mem_save` — a validated selection that eliminates project drift. **D2 fork rulings PINNED: cursor=git-ref refs/governance/audit-cursor, channel=stdout [FAIL-SHA] single-parser, exit-2=A4 null-doctrine per-check both-fixtures**

**What**: Owner rulings on the 3 D2 design forks, PINNED before sdd-design (design starts fixed, does not reopen these).

**Cross-cutting theme (design MUST make explicit)**: EVERY D2 decision is made with the GitLab port as the future consumer — D2 is the slice that LIFTS the "no postmerge to GitLab" restriction, so nothing may be born coupled to GitHub. This is the m3-class-coupling test applied to every choice.

**FORK 1 — Cursor: a CUSTOM GIT REF `refs/governance/audit-cursor`.** Not tag, not marker file, not Actions cache. Why: Actions-cache is ephemeral AND GitHub-only (would couple the cursor to the platform exactly when D2 exists to unblock GitLab — m3 again); a committed marker file = the postmerge writing to `main` on every advance (noise + the auto-loop class this slice kills). A custom ref is git-native, invisible to the normal workflow, pushable, identical on both platforms. RECOVERY if missing: NO auto-init — cursor absent → exit 2 + LOUD issue carrying the documented init instruction (explicit command, human keystroke). Bootstrapping the mechanism that opens automatic reverts is a human decision, never a silent default (lesson of the cascade).

**FORK 2 — Channel: STDOUT with a parseable marker.** Confirms the propose lean. GITHUB_OUTPUT discarded for the same reason as cache (platform-specific with the port pending). Strict machine format: one line per SHA, fixed prefix `[FAIL-SHA] <sha>`. Parsing lives in ONE tested function that BOTH wrappers (GitHub today, GitLab tomorrow) consume — the never-a-second-parser rule: ZERO inline grep in the YAML.

**FORK 3 — exit-2 boundary: the A4 null=uncomputable doctrine elevated to an exit code.** Discriminator: did the evaluator RECEIVE its inputs and evaluate? → computed verdict = 0 or 1. Could it NOT compute? (git failed, adapter threw, a required input absent/unreadable) → 2. Two locks against the escape-hatch: (a) exit 2 is ALWAYS loud (labeled issue, never suppressible) — a silent 2 does not exist; (b) the drift-guard requires EVERY check to ship BOTH fixtures — one genuine violation (→1) and one uncomputable (→2) — so the boundary is pinned per-check IN TESTS, not by implementer judgment. Corollary: every catch-all of unexpected exceptions maps to 2 (fail-loud), never 0 or 1 (misattribution).

content:
**sdd/issue-259-d2/design**

**What**: DESIGN remediation (§15, appended to design.md) for the D2 PR3 judgment-day R3 CONFIRMED CRITICAL — revert-of-revert laundering (audit goes GREEN while an ungoverned ADR sits at HEAD).

**Core fix — net-tip-effect anchoring.** Replace the PAIRWISE existence test in resolution.mjs isResolvedAt (`∃ merge R∈(O,tip]: normDiff(R,R^1)==normDiff(O^1,O)`) with a signed NET-PARITY count over the same `--first-parent --merges` candidate set, reusing normDiff as the per-comparison kernel (so ALL PR2 properties — rename/copy fail-closed, whitespace-exact, --binary/--no-ext-diff hardening — carry over unchanged; only the aggregator changes from ∃ to signed count). Two predicates, ranges differ BY DESIGN:
- resolved-skip (pre-eval, wholesale): DIRECTIONAL — `netPresent(O)=1+Σ_{W∈(O,tip]} sign(W,dO) ≤ 0` → resolved. Counting only merges AFTER O keeps the HEAD-most merge never wholesale-skipped, preserving the memoryPresence global-gap invariant.
- reverter-skip (post-fail, partial tree-keyed exempt): FULL-WINDOW — `netAddFull(C)=|{W:fW==dC}|−|{W:fW==dCinv}| ≤ 0`. Full range lets a HEAD-most cleanup revert see the offender behind it; keeps TREE_KEYED_CHECKS restriction so its memoryPresence still runs.
sign(W,s)=+1 if fW==s (re-add), −1 if fW==dCinv (invert), 0 else (rename matches neither → fail-closed). Worked: O,R → netPresent 0 resolved (liveness); O,R,R2 → netPresent +1 NOT resolved, R2 flagged+[FAIL-SHA] (THE FIX); O,R,R2,R3 → 0 resolved (no over-correction).

**Fork decision: OPTION A** (fix inside resolution.mjs, reopen merged PR2) over B (wiring-layer gate). Reasons: the defect IS the predicate definition (existence vs net); one place holds the invariant; every consumer (GitLab wrapper, future checks) inherits correctness; cold-reviewer verifies "is re-introduction resolved?" in ONE function. Echoes PR2-R1 precedent, follows D-2 "prefer the theorem to the check." Cost: re-touches feature/v2.0.0 PR2 surface, ripples to A2/A5 fixtures — small (kernel untouched).

**[FAIL-SHA] contract: class-FILTERED at emitter (not class-carrying at consumer).** Emit iff merge has ≥1 un-exempted TREE-KEYED failure (adrPresence/diffSize); issueLink/memoryPresence NEVER emit (re-eval/human-gate classes per REQ-D2-10a). Plus newest-net-present-carrier dedup per payload (attack: O and R2 share dO; only R2 emits → PR4 reverts live carrier once, never resurrects O/R). Closes WARNING doubly: (1) global memoryPresence gap → [FAIL] exit 1 but zero [FAIL-SHA], no mass auto-revert; (2) partial reverter-skip R failing only issueLink → no [FAIL-SHA], O not resurrected. Requires crossCheckExit change: split failCount (any [FAIL]) from [FAIL-SHA] count; exit 1 ⟺ failCount≥1, [FAIL-SHA] MAY be 0 on exit 1.

**Minor rulings**: (a) adrPresence [FAIL] carries human-gate remediation (accept --reason) — no automatic forward-fix path. (b) DELETE isOffender gate (brain-audit.mjs:148) — Judge B proved keep-justification unreachable AND the net-parity restructure removes the whole isReverterOf/isOffender enumeration it lived in.

**Spec drift flagged**: REQ-D2-10 has TWO defects (still describes stale path-scoped `P∩D=∅` that PR2-R1 already replaced with diff-inversion; AND needs net-tip anchor). REQ-D2-10a (P∩D→net + [FAIL-SHA] class filter), REQ-D2-6(b) (code==1 ⇒ ≥1 [FAIL] not [FAIL-SHA]), REQ-D2-3 (per auto-revertible merge, deduped). NEW REQ-D2-16 (net-tip-effect invariant). §7.1 extended with A7 (revert-of-revert), A8 (even chain settles/liveness), A9 (class-filtered [FAIL-SHA]) — each must redden against BOTH eff4560 ancestry AND the pairwise PR2 predicate.

**Where**: openspec/changes/issue-259-d2/design.md §15 (appended EOF) + 2 pointer notes at §3.3/§3.6; grounded in resolution.mjs:133-207, brain-audit.mjs:43-59/145-208/450-498, spec.md REQ-D2-10/10a/6/3.

content:
**Fixed verify-change failure on deleted files**

**What**: Filtered files by existence (`existsSync(join(ROOT, f))`) in the `scripts` check of `verify-change.mjs` before executing `node --check` or `bash -n`.
**Why**: When files are deleted in a branch (like `chunk-reader.mjs` was in a previous issue), `git diff` still lists them as changed. Without this filter, `node --check` attempts to read the missing file, throwing `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and breaking quality validation for the branch.
**Where**: brain/scripts/verify-change.mjs
**Learned**: `git diff --name-only` includes deleted files. Command evaluators that run per-file checks must always verify physical existence on disk.

**R-1 CORRECTION (caught by adversarial review, D2 Slice 1 F3): automatic cursor resolution = trailer in a commit that is a verified DESCENDANT of M, not substring over the window**

**CORRECTION to R-1 (the cursor dual-path resolution ruling), forced by finding F3 in the D2 Slice 1 adversarial review.**

R-1 originally: automatic resolution = the `This reverts commit <sha>.` trailer detected in the window. The Slice-1 impl did this as a SUBSTRING match over all concatenated commit bodies in the range (`cursor.mjs:76` `isRevertedInRange`). F3 proved that is BYPASSABLE: a follow-up commit whose body contains a FAKE `This reverts commit <M>.` trailer (naming M's now-known sha, with no real revert) falsely marks M "resolved" → the cursor advances past M → M is never reverted. That is EXACTLY the cursor-advance-without-resolution that D2 exists to make impossible.

**FINAL R-1 (hardened):** automatic resolution counts ONLY if the `This reverts commit <M>.` trailer lives in a commit that is a VERIFIED DESCENDANT of M — the real revert git generated — checked by ANCESTRY (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <M> <candidate>` AND candidate ≠ M), never by substring over arbitrary window bodies. The manual `accept`-with-reason path (the human gate) is unchanged and remains the SECOND path.

**Why not "accept and lean on the human gate":** rejected for the same reason F2 was — a soft mitigation over an available structural fix. The hardening IS the fix. The adversarial test MUST include the case: a follow-up commit with a fake trailer does NOT advance the cursor.

**Meta-lesson:** a "pinned" ruling can still carry a latent wrong assumption (here: "a revert trailer implies a real revert"). The fresh adversarial review is what surfaced it — the implementer's green suite did not. Supersedes the automatic-path detail in [[sdd/issue-259-d2/fork-rulings]] (#879) and the R-1 line in this topic (#886). Related: [[doctrine/mechanical-gates-catch-what-review-cannot]].

**Finding (base): baptism #258 chunk-reader retirement left a dangling entry in verify-change.mjs's node --check list → brain:change:verify RED on feature/v2.0.0**

**What**: `brain:change:verify` (`brain/scripts/verify-change.mjs`) is RED on the base branch `feature/v2.0.0`. Verified independently on a clean detached worktree of `origin/feature/v2.0.0`: `node brain/scripts/verify-change.mjs issue-256-b2` → `Error: Cannot find module '.../brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs'`. verify-change runs `node --check` over a static list of script files that STILL includes `brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs` and `chunk-reader.test.mjs` — but the baptism (#258) DELETED those files. So the static list dangles.

**Why it matters**: this is the SECOND straggler from #258's chunk-reader retirement (the first was a cosmetic dangling comment in `store.mjs:132-133`). This one is worse — it breaks a GATE (`brain:change:verify`) on the integration branch for every SDD change. `npm test` stays green (the deleted files aren't imported by any live module), which is why the baptism's suite passed and missed it — the only surface that trips is verify-change's static `node --check` list.

**Where**: `brain/scripts/verify-change.mjs` (the static file list feeding `node --check`); the deleted `brain/scripts/lib/chunk-reader.mjs` + `.test.mjs`. Also the cosmetic comment in `brain/scripts/memory/lib/store.mjs:132-133`.

**Fix direction**: remove the two dangling `chunk-reader` entries from verify-change.mjs's check list (+ optionally the store.mjs comment). Small, but it needs its own approved issue (L5 order — [[doctrine/l5-order-not-exempted-by-urgency]]). Candidate for the micro-batch, but GATE-BREAKING so higher priority within it. NOT in D2's scope (D2 = auto-revert guardrails; scope discipline holds).

**What**: Design doc for converting the human-mediated external reviewer (CP-* checkpoints) into an invocable cold agent. Written to design-docs/reviewer-protocol-claude-code.md (untracked).

**Design-off measurement: two harnesses, same brief — complementary blind spots (the n>1 harness argument) — Track H (#266)**

**What**: Ran a controlled design-off — identical brief (design the automated external reviewer protocol), two harnesses (Claude Code, Antigravity) working in isolation, no cross-reading. Verdict: SYNTHESIS (Claude skeleton + 3 Antigravity transplants + 3 documented rejections). Became issue #266.

**TRACK LETTER — CORRECTED: it is Track H, not Track G and not Track R.** The kickoff called it "Track G", but `docs/inbox/PLAN-adapters-v3.md:418` already assigns G to `brain:metrics` (CP-G1). Letters A–G are taken; H is the first free letter in order. Ruled Track H, phases H0–H2, recorded as a PLAN-DEVIATION in the issue body. (An earlier version of this observation said "Track R" — that was wrong and is now superseded.)

This is the THIRD track-letter churn in a week (Distribution→D, then G collision, then this correction), which re-proves [[track-letters-uncontrolled-namespace]]: the durable fix is a canonical letter→name→status table in the plan, where opening a track means taking the next free letter AND registering it in the same act.

**Why (the meta-measurement — the point of the experiment)**: two harnesses, same brief, complementary blind spots. Claude was **structural-governmental**: it found the authorization hazard by reading the gates (`brain:protect` sets `required_approving_review_count: 1`; L6 counts any non-author APPROVE — so a reviewer agent running `gh pr review --approve` would become a merge authorizer), and produced the three structural locks (COMMENT-state verdicts, a verb with no approve code path, `governance.approvalActors`). Antigravity was **operational-concrete**: TDD-RED validation by reversion, real CI hosting (`reviewer.yml` + per-PR concurrency mutex), cross-PR sequencing board.

Neither harness found what the other found. The union covered what neither covered alone. **This is the sharpest empirical argument we have for n>1 harnesses** — not a preference, a measurement.

**Where**: issue #266. Both source documents preserved unmodified as the record of the experiment: `design-docs/reviewer-protocol-claude-code.md` (15,210 B) and `design-docs/reviewer-protocol-antigravity.md` (8,296 B), currently untracked in the main worktree, durably backed up at `~/.claude/projects/-home-gandalf-IA-brain/design-docs/`. They get committed together, as-is, on the Track H branch.

**Learned**: the Antigravity doc was originally written inside the `brain-issue-260` worktree, which is slated for post-merge cleanup after #261 — deliverables written inside a disposable worktree are one `git worktree remove` away from being lost. Rescued before cleanup. Worktree-local untracked files are not a storage location.

**Status**: #266 is OPEN with the full synthesis in its body (H0/H1/H2 scope, transplants, rejections, failure modes, acceptance). It carries `type:feature` but NOT `status:approved` — human approval is the L5 gate that must precede any branch.

content:
**Track letters are an uncontrolled namespace — two real collisions in a week; needs a canonical assignment table**

**What**: Track letters in docs/inbox/PLAN-adapters-v3.md are a namespace with NO canonical registry, and they have now collided twice in one week: (1) "Track D" — Distribution vs the PLAN's D (Governance hardening); (2) "Track G" — the automated external reviewer kickoff vs the PLAN's G (Process metrics, PLAN-adapters-v3.md:418).

**Why it happens**: a track is opened by writing a new "## N. Track X" heading in the plan. Nothing enumerates the taken letters, nothing reserves the next one, and the plan is long enough (518 lines) that a new track author reasonably guesses instead of scanning. The collision surfaces only if someone greps.

**The ruling that closed collision #2**: enumerate ALL assigned letters against the plan with evidence, then take the FIRST FREE LETTER IN ORDER — never a mnemonic letter (rejected "Track R for Reviewer": it breaks the plan's sequential scheme and leaves an alphabetical hole that invites the NEXT collision). Assigned: A(:96) B(:183) C(:252) D(:313) E(:352) F(:385) G(:418); `rg '\bTrack [H-Z]\b'` → no matches. Chose **Track H** (issue #266).

**The durable fix (micro-slice candidate, not yet an issue)**: the plan should carry ONE canonical table — letter → name → status — as the single source of truth for the namespace, and "open a track" must mean "take the next free letter from that table AND register it there in the same act". Same doctrine brain already applies elsewhere: a single accessor over a scattered literal (cf. sdd-layout.mjs owning REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS, governance-checks.mjs owning the job names, each with a drift-guard test). A track table without a taken-and-registered-in-one-act rule is just another scattered literal.

**Interim mitigation**: record the collision as a PLAN-DEVIATION inside the issue (done in #266) — the plan's own escape hatch for "reality contradicts this plan" (PLAN-adapters-v3.md:495-498).

**Learned**: this is the third instance of the same brain-wide pattern — a load-bearing name with no single source of truth drifts (governance job names → drift-guard test; SDD required artifacts → sdd-layout.mjs; track letters → nothing yet). The pattern is the finding, not the letter.</content>

- Base-branch mechanism ALREADY EXISTS: `config?.project?.defaultBranch ?? 'main'` (brain-ship.mjs:157, brain-governance-status.mjs:59/106/265) + `--base` flag (ticket-start.mjs:30). Isolated into its own PR slice so the gate diff is reviewed on merit.

content:
**Judgment Day Round 1 — Slice 1 issue-259-d2 NOT shippable: F3 fix is theater, cursor ref never fetched**

**What**: Blind dual adversarial review (judgment-day, Judge A + Judge B, both opus) of the Slice 1 diff for issue-259-d2 on branch feat/issue-259-fixgovernance-d2-rung-3-auto-revert-guar (8 commits, origin/feature/v2.0.0..HEAD). Verdict: NOT APPROVED. 3 confirmed CRITICALs, 6 confirmed real WARNINGs. Both judges reproduced the top findings empirically in scratch repos, not just by reading.

**Why**: Pre-push gate after a fix-forward pass that claimed to close 5 prior findings (F1/F2/F3/F5 + doc drift). The judges were told NOT to take those fixes on faith. Two of them do not hold.

**CONFIRMED CRITICAL (both judges, both reproduced):**
1. **F3 is NOT fixed — ancestry check is security theater.** `isRevertedInRange` (cursor.mjs:102-114) trusts a candidate when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <offender> <candidate>` succeeds. But on a linear main, EVERY commit merged after the offender is its descendant. The check only rules out a lineage forked BEFORE the offender — a shape that never occurs in normal PR flow, and the only shape the tests cover. Real attack, reproduced by both judges: land offender M, then land an ordinary PR whose commit body says "This reverts commit <M-sha>." and reverts nothing. Ancestry passes → brain-audit prints `[SKIP] ... resolved by revert` → no revert PR → cursor advances past M forever. The offender's payload is still on disk. The `candidate !== sha` guard is dead code (a commit body cannot contain its own full sha). Ancestry is necessary but nowhere near sufficient; proving a revert requires checking the TREE EFFECT (offender's diff inverted between M and candidate), not a trailer + ancestry.
2. **`refs/governance/audit-cursor` is NEVER fetched into the runner.** `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0` sets `remote.origin.fetch = +refs/heads/*` (+tags) only; custom ref namespaces are not fetched, and no step in the workflow fetches `refs/governance/*`. So: schedule runs → readCursor always fails → missingCursor → loud issue + exit 1 EVERY DAY forever, even after a human correctly initializes the ref on origin (daily backstop permanently dead). Push runs → cursor-precheck always emits `cursor_exists=false` → the advance step never runs and a "cursor missing" issue is filed on every clean push. The F2 fix is net-NEGATIVE in production: before it, update-ref would (wrongly) bootstrap the ref but keep the mechanism alive; now the cursor is permanently dead and REQ-D2-1/REQ-D2-2 are non-functional. Fix: `git fetch origin '+refs/governance/*:refs/governance/*'` after checkout.
3. **Window-step crash fails OPEN into a clean audit.** governance-postmerge.yml:35-50 — the `node -e` promise chain has no `.catch()` and runs under `set +e`. Any throw → non-zero exit, EMPTY stdout → `result=""` → not "MISSING" → writes `missing_cursor=false` and an EMPTY `range=`. Audit then runs `brain-audit.mjs ""` → resolveRange falls back to `origin/main..HEAD` → empty range on a push to main → `[INFO] No merge commits found` → EXIT 0. An infra failure silently becomes a governance PASS, and the cursor advances. Textbook fail-open on the exact compute path R-2 was meant to harden.

**CONFIRMED WARNING (real) — both judges:**
4. Crashed brain-audit → GREEN job. Top-level catch exits 1 (not 2); crash text goes to stderr which `out=$(node ...)` does not capture → AUDIT_STDOUT empty → parse-failures yields 0 offenders → loop body never runs → step exits 0. Also: `set -o pipefail` does NOT propagate out of process substitution `< <(...)`, so a failing parse-failures.mjs leaves mapfile at status 0 with an empty array. Exit codes >= 3 / SIGKILL match no `if:` → all steps skip → job green.
5. Dedup keyed on the BRANCH, and the branch is pushed BEFORE `gh pr create`. If PR creation fails (rate limit, network, missing label) the orphan branch survives → every later run hits the `already exists ... skipping` guard → the revert PR is NEVER created, job green forever. Key on the PR (`gh pr list --head`), not the branch.
6. `git revert` conflict aborts the whole loop under `set -euo pipefail`. Offenders 2..N silently dropped, no `--abort`, no issue, and it re-conflicts on every rerun — one poisoned offender blocks all others indefinitely.
7. **The loud-issue labels do not exist.** `gh label list` returns only `size:exception`. Neither `governance:cursor-missing` nor `governance:audit-uncomputable` exists, `gh issue create --label <nonexistent>` FAILS, and all three call sites are `|| true`'d → the labelled issue REQ-D2-2/R-2 mandates is never created. Worse: the F2 fix's OWN loud path (yml:136-143) has `|| true` and NO `exit 1` → step succeeds → job GREEN, zero signal. The F2 "loud" branch is a no-op.
8. **The test suite rewrites the developer's git identity.** release-postmerge-workflows.test.mjs (~line 398): `probeScript` is built from `scriptLines.slice(0, mapfileIdx+1)`, which INCLUDES the workflow's `git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"` / `user.email` lines, and is run via `spawnSync('bash', ...)` with NO `cwd` → executes in `process.cwd()`. Both judges reproduced it: running `npm test` silently overwrites the local git identity of the worktree. This is almost certainly why this worktree's `Git user` reads `github-actions[bot]`. Also cwd-coupled: the test FAILS from any cwd other than repo root (relative `node brain/scripts/...` path).
9. Record framing `%H\x1f%B\x1e` is not injection-proof — git permits \x1e/\x1f in commit messages (both judges verified round-trip). The code comment claiming otherwise is false. Grants no new power today (F3 is trivially exploitable anyway) but will silently defeat any CORRECT future hardening built on this parse. Use `git log -z` / `%x00` (NUL is the one byte git cannot store).

**SUSPECT (Judge B only, not independently confirmed):**
- **Cursor skip-over (B rates CRITICAL)**: `resolveWindow` on a PUSH ignores the cursor (`range = before..head`), but the workflow advances the cursor to `github.sha` on any exit 0. Audited window != cursor target. Push P1 lands offender M (exit 1, cursor stays at C); push P2 lands a clean merge, window `M..P2` EXCLUDES M (git log A..B is exclusive of A) → exit 0 → cursor jumps to P2, over M. If the revert PR is never merged, M is never audited again. Defeats REQ-D2-1's "advance only on a clean verdict". Needs independent confirmation.
- Infinite auto-revert loop: the auto-revert merge is itself audited next window; adrPresence sees the offender's same file set → revert gets flagged → revert-of-revert. No skip class for `auto-revert/*`.
- No `concurrency:` group — parallel schedule+push runs race on the revert branch and can push the cursor BACKWARD (GitHub does not enforce fast-forward on non-refs/heads refs).
- The "never auto-create" invariant lives in YAML, not in the platform-neutral core — `advanceCursor` still calls bare `git update-ref` (creates if absent). Directly contradicts the design's "ALL decision logic in the core, a GitLab wrapper calls it UNCHANGED" — a GitLab wrapper would re-introduce F2 verbatim. Fix belongs in the core as an atomic CAS `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`.
- `grep -c '^parent '` on `git cat-file -p` also matches commit-MESSAGE lines starting with "parent " → inflated parent_count.

**STRICT TDD VERDICT — the tests do not prove what they claim (both judges):**
- F3 tests are SELF-CONFIRMING: cursor.test.mjs:128 just makes a fake `merge-base` throw; brain-audit.test.mjs:485 forks the attacker branch from `rootSha` (i.e. BEFORE the offender) — the one shape the fix handles. Neither tests the realistic fork-after-offender case, which both judges proved still passes. The tests would go green against a fix that does nothing useful — which is exactly what happened.
- F2 execution test is TAUTOLOGICAL: it asserts rev-parse fails in a temp repo with no ref — the same output the BROKEN production path produces. It cannot distinguish "correctly gated" from "ref never fetched so the gate always trips".
- F1 execution test is half theatre: part 1 hand-builds the vulnerable bash string itself rather than executing pre-fix code. Part 2 (extracting the real mapfile line) has teeth. F1 structural tests are legit.

**CONFIRMED GOOD:**
- F1 (CWE-94) genuinely fixed for the shell-injection class: no `run:` block splices `steps.audit.outputs.stdout`; both consumers route via `env: AUDIT_STDOUT` and reference `"$AUDIT_STDOUT"` double-quoted. Residue is only `${{ github.sha }}` (pure hex, not attacker-controlled) and a `$RANDOM` heredoc delimiter.
- F5 fixed: `br="auto-revert/${sha}"` full 40-hex; parse-failures enforces `^\[FAIL-SHA\] ([0-9a-f]{40})$`. Only remaining truncation is the cosmetic `${sha:0:7}` in the PR title.
- Doc drift fixed: spec.md REQ-D2-5 now under Slice 1, matching design.md.
- **397 counted lines INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by both judges** (workflow 165 + brain-audit.mjs 44 + cursor.mjs 148 + parse-failures.mjs 40; all *.test.mjs and openspec/changes/** correctly excluded by governance.ignoreList). Judge B computed it through the repo's OWN parseDiffNumstat + brain.config.json. No size:exception.

**Learned**:
- **Only 3 lines of headroom under the 400-line budget.** Every confirmed fix above adds code. The budget is the binding constraint on the remediation, and Judge B's read is that "3 lines of headroom is itself a signal that Slice 1 is packed too tight". Re-slicing is likely required — a fix-forward in place cannot fit.
- The two CRITICALs are DESIGN-level, not patch-level: (a) a revert cannot be proven by trailer + ancestry, only by tree effect; (b) the cursor ref's fetch was never part of the design at all. Neither is a typo — both survived a prior fix-forward pass AND its tests, because the tests were written to the same wrong mental model as the code.
- Meta-lesson: the fix-forward pass wrote tests that encode the FIXER'S threat model rather than the attacker's. Self-confirming tests are worse than no tests — they converted "unverified" into "verified green" while the hole stayed open.

content:
**Doctrine: a regression test is derived from the ATTACK, not the fix — must redden against a plausible-but-wrong fix**

**What**: A security/regression test for a finding MUST be derived from the ATTACK, never from the fix. Its acceptance bar is NOT "it fails without the fix" — it is "it ALSO FAILS against a plausible-but-wrong fix." Corollary: the adversarial tests for a finding are written by whoever FOUND it, or by an independent third party — NEVER by the author of the patch.

**Why**: Owner-issued doctrine, born from issue-259-d2. The fix-forward pass for F3 hardened a forgeable revert-trailer by adding a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` check and shipped tests that went GREEN — but the tests only ever constructed the ONE scenario the fix handled (an attacker lineage forked BEFORE the offender), which never occurs in normal linear-main PR flow. They never constructed the realistic attack (fork AFTER the offender, where every commit is trivially a descendant), which the ancestry check does nothing to stop. So the tests passed against a fix that does nothing useful. The F2 test was worse — tautological: it asserted `git rev-parse` fails in a repo with no ref, which is EXACTLY the output the BROKEN production path also produces (the ref was never fetched), so it could not distinguish "correctly gated" from "permanently dead." Self-confirming tests are worse than no tests: they convert "unverified" into "verified green" while the hole stays open.

**Root cause pattern**: the patch author writes tests from their OWN threat model (the silla del que arregla / the fixer's chair), which is the same wrong mental model that produced the broken fix. The test and the code share the blind spot, so they agree.

**How to apply**:
1. For each security-relevant requirement, state in the design WHAT AN ADVERSARIAL FIXTURE MUST CONSTRUCT to prove it — not just what a happy-path test asserts.
2. Every adversarial test must be shown to REDDEN against the prior plausible-but-wrong fix (e.g. the ancestry-only fix), not merely against un-fixed code. If it stays green against the wrong fix, it is not a proof.
3. Do not let the person writing the patch also author its adversarial fixtures. Finder or third party derives them.

This is generalizable beyond brain — it is a testing doctrine. Related: [[sdd/issue-259-d2/judgment-round-1]], [[decision/issue-259-d2-R1-replacement-tree-effect]].

**RULING: R-1 REPLACED — auto revert-resolution = tree effect, never trailer/ancestry; chain = stacked-to-main 5 PRs**

**What**: Two owner rulings on issue-259-d2 after judgment-day escalation.

**RULING 1 — R-1 REPLACED (owner self-correction, second time).** The prior R-1 ruling (harden F3 by `git merge-base --is-ancestor` ancestry) was THEATER and is withdrawn. Both judges were right: on a linear main every commit merged after offender M descends from M, so ancestry proves nothing. The owner named the failure explicitly: reasoned the mechanism from the fixer's chair, not the attacker's — the same class of error that produced the self-confirming tests. New binding rule:
- Automatic revert-resolution = **TREE EFFECT ONLY**: the offender's touched paths are byte-identical to their pre-offender state at HEAD, plus an anti-vacuity guard. NEVER by commit trailer, NEVER by ancestry.
- The trailer is REMOVED from the design as a discriminator entirely (not a hint, not a filter).
- The **human gate** (registered/recorded acceptance) remains as the SECOND and only other resolution path.

**RULING 2 — chain strategy = STACKED-TO-MAIN, 5 PRs.** Each PR merges to feature/v2.0.0 in order, each <400 counted lines, no size:exception. Consistent with the previously-confirmed stacked-to-main for the original 2-slice split. feature-branch-chain is rejected on its own cost: the tracker's integration PR into feature/v2.0.0 would be a single ~700-line diff requiring the size:exception the proposal explicitly FORBIDS. Owner's framing: "the new mechanism being born asking for the very exception its own doctrine forbids is self-contradiction, not a trade-off."

**OPEN adversarial question the owner mandated design.md must ANSWER (not assume)**: does "tree-effect resolution" cover ALL violation classes brain-audit can flag, or only CONTENT classes? If a class exists whose resolution is NOT "paths restored to pre-offender" (e.g. a presence/metadata violation resolved by ADDING something, not restoring), that class has no automatic path and must fall EXPLICITLY to the human gate or exit-2 — never a false "resolved." design.md must enumerate the violation classes and map each one.

**Why**: pre-push remediation after the Slice 1 diff was escalated (obs #899). These rulings drive the design v2 (obs #881) and the forthcoming re-slice + tasks.

**Where**: openspec/changes/issue-259-d2/design.md, brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/cursor.mjs, brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs.

content:
**Ruling 1 verdict: the identity-poisoning test is D2's OWN (not env) — isolation born-in-PR4, PR1-3 run full suite**

**What**: Owner Ruling 1 on issue-259-d2, VERIFIED with file:line evidence. The claim "the full npm test suite cannot be run from the real worktree until PR4 (test-harness isolation)" is NOT an environment property — it is a consequence of D2's own slicing. env-limits-not-world-properties (the recorder lesson).

**Evidence (git, measured not assumed):**
- `origin/feature/v2.0.0:brain/scripts/vcs/release-postmerge-workflows.test.mjs` = 145 lines, NO `probeScript`, NO F1 execution-level test, NO identity poisoning. `git grep github-actions[bot] origin/feature/v2.0.0 -- '*.test.mjs'` finds NO test setting it as a real git identity (only a `ci.provider` string in installer.test:127). The base is clean.
- `scrap/d2-v1-broken` (the 8 discarded D2 commits) = 497 lines of the same file. `git diff origin/feature/v2.0.0 scrap/d2-v1-broken` shows D2 ADDED the poison: `release-postmerge-workflows.test.mjs:317-318` — `const probeScript = scriptLines.slice(0, mapfileIdx+1)...; spawnSync('bash', ['-c', probeScript], {` with NO `cwd`. The extracted workflow lines include `git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"`, so it runs in the repo cwd and rewrites the dev identity. The SAME commit's precheck test at :378-379 DID pass `cwd: dir` — it knew how to isolate and didn't here.
- HEAD (reset branch) = 145 lines = base. The poisoning test is NOT present on the current branch. Running `npm test` on the reset branch is SAFE.

**Resolution (owner ruling): a known hazard is NOT introduced in PR-N to isolate it in PR-N+3.** The isolation lands WITH or BEFORE the code that needs it (same principle as R-2: a new mechanism never born fail-open).
- The poisoning test only exists because it tests the workflow (it extracts `run:` blocks from `.github/workflows/governance-postmerge.yml` via `scriptLines.slice`), so it is genuinely COUPLED to PR4 (the workflow rewrite) — it cannot be extracted to PR0/PR1 because there is no workflow to test before then. Coupling proven by evidence, per the owner's "if genuinely coupled, demonstrate and I re-evaluate."
- But coupled-to-PR4 does NOT license "broken in PR4, fixed in PR4 phase 4.0 later." PR4's workflow-extracting tests are BORN ISOLATED: every `spawnSync('bash', extracted)` runs with `cwd: <temp repo>` + `env: { GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null', GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM: '/dev/null' }` from its first RED. The D1/D2 guard is written INTO the test, not a follow-up. Zero hazard window.
- Therefore PR1, PR2, PR3 do NOT introduce the test → they have NO hazard → they run the FULL suite normally. The tasks.md "scope tests to own files in PR1-3 / can't run suite until PR4" constraint is a PHANTOM (it assumed re-introducing the broken test early) and is REMOVED.

**Asymmetry the owner noted (reduces risk, does NOT justify order):** the REVIEWER runs the full suite in a disposable worktree (never commits) and CI runs local-checks per PR, so full-suite verification is covered regardless of local scoping.

**Action**: tasks.md corrected (remove phantom constraint; mandate born-isolated PR4 test; PR1-3 full suite). PR1 apply proceeds and may run the full suite.

Related: [[sdd/issue-259-d2/apply-progress]], [[decision/issue-259-d2-R1-replacement-tree-effect]], [[doctrine/adversarial-test-derivation]].

content:
**H0-LOCK3-DUAL resolved: split governance.approvalActors into two single-semantic keys (reviewActors for L6, approvalActors for L5)**

**What**: Human decision resolving blocker `H0-LOCK3-DUAL` in Track H (#266, automated external reviewer). Chosen: **option (a) — split the single `governance.approvalActors` key into two keys, each with exactly one semantic, each read by exactly one gate.**

1. `governance.reviewActors` (NEW) — "these identities do NOT count as the human reviewer." Read ONLY by L6 (`brain-writes-reviewed.mjs`): the human-approver search excludes `author + reviewActors`. The reviewer handle registers HERE and only here.
2. `governance.approvalActors` (EXISTING, semantics unchanged) — "these identities MAY legitimately apply `status:approved`." Read ONLY by L5 (`actor-check.mjs`). The reviewer handle NEVER appears here.

No key feeds two gates. Two mandatory tests gate the landing (decision does not land without both): (t1) reviewer identity does NOT pass `actor-check` when applying `status:approved`; (t2) reviewer identity IS excluded from the L6 human-approver count. Final key names are a design.md detail, closed at spec review.

**Why (the hazard the split dissolves)**: The reviewer (`brain-review/1` rev 1 verdict) found that `governance.approvalActors` today feeds `botAllowlist` in BOTH gates with OPPOSITE semantics — restrictive at L6 (an allowlisted APPROVE does not count as the human review) but PERMISSIVE at L5 (`actor-check.evaluateActor` returns `{level:'pass', reason:'allow-listed automation identity'}` for an allowlisted actor applying `status:approved`). Registering the reviewer handle in that one key would de-authorize it at L6 AND simultaneously authorize it to self-apply `status:approved` at L5 — falsifying the draft's claim that "actor-check independently catches a misapplied status:approved" (for THIS identity it would bless it), leaving the caller deny-set as the ONLY lock = exactly the "rule the agent remembers" config the draft declares insufficient. Splitting the key dissolves the dual-semantics coupling by construction, not by convention.

**Where (citations — this record's authority)**:
- Finding + code evidence: issue #266 comment https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain/issues/266#issuecomment-4974795208 (brain-review/1 rev 1, finding H0-LOCK3-DUAL, cold-clone evidence at feature/v2.0.0@3174492d).
- Human decision: issue #266 comment https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain/issues/266#issuecomment-4975121847 (csrinaldi, 2026-07-14: "la separación de la lista en dos es la correcta").
- Code touched at implementation: `brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs` (L5 evaluateActor botAllowlist pass branch), `brain/scripts/vcs/brain-writes-reviewed.mjs` (L6 humanApprover / defaultReadBotAllowlist), `brain.config.json` (governance keys).

**Learned**: The rev-1 verdict is REVISE, not APPROVE — H0-LOCK3-DUAL is resolved but OTHER conditions remain open before #266 can get `status:approved`: (1) H0-VERBS-WRITE wording — "none of the 16 verbs write" is false (`mrCreate`, `branchProtect` write); correct to "none write to the review/comment/label surface"; (2) carried track-letter conditions (PLAN on a server-visible ref; meta-finding record location; transplant count reconciled — body says 4, report said 3). Belongs to Track H H0 ADR. Related: [[track-letters-uncontrolled-namespace]], the #896 design-off measurement.

**Process note**: this decision lived ONLY in a chat conversation for ~a day and was invisible to a cold clone reading the server — a real reviewer-protocol defect (verdict/decision must live in the server thread, not chat). Now corrected: both are server-visible comments. Separately, a cold reader must fetch the full thread (`gh issue view --comments`), not `--json body` alone — the body projection never returns comments.

content:
**Judgment-day PR1 (cursor core): no CRITICAL, CAS+tri-state PROVEN real by both judges; 1 confirmed WARNING = remote-CAS leg untested (doctrine gap)**

**What**: Blind dual adversarial review (judgment-day, Judge A + Judge B, both opus) of PR1 of issue-259-d2 (the platform-neutral tri-state cursor + CAS core: git-seam.mjs + cursor.mjs, commits f57e1f4/b684652/39c3791, 193 counted lines). Verdict: NO CRITICAL. Both owner-flagged mechanisms PROVEN functionally real by execution, independently by both judges. One confirmed real WARNING (a doctrine-level test gap), two proven single-judge WARNINGs, several low-severity items.

**PROVEN REAL (both judges, by execution — the opposite of the ancestry theater):**
- CAS is genuine on BOTH legs. Both judges built a two-clone fixture and proved `push --force-with-lease=refs/governance/audit-cursor:<from>` with the explicit expected value REJECTS a stale lease (`! [rejected] ... (stale info)`, rc=1) when the remote moved between read and swap. Local `update-ref <ref> <to> <from>` is a genuine CAS and refuses to create an absent ref. advanceCursor.from is explicit → real. acceptManually's RACE test (cursor.test.mjs:299) genuinely reddens against the pre-fix internal-read variant.
- Tri-state is sound. `ls-remote --exit-code` returns 2 ONLY for genuine absence on a reachable remote; nonexistent remote/path, DNS-invalid, unreachable → 128 → 'unknown'; signal-kill/ENOENT → status -1 → 'unknown'. No infra failure maps to 'absent'. status===2 stable across git versions.

**CONFIRMED real WARNING (both judges) — MUST fix before PR1's PR:**
- **Remote CAS leg has ZERO discriminating test coverage.** cursor.test.mjs:222 (B5) and :299 (RACE) both run in a SINGLE workdir, so the LOCAL update-ref CAS (cursor.mjs:75) short-circuits and throws before the remote push (cursor.mjs:77) is ever reached. Both judges proved the remote CAS WORKS via a two-clone fixture, but NO shipped test exercises the rejection — a regression that breaks the lease (plain `--force`, or `--force-with-lease=<ref>` WITHOUT the explicit `:<from>`, which compares against the remote-tracking ref and is always satisfied post-fetch) stays GREEN. This is precisely the self-confirming-test gap doctrine #900 forbids, on the security-critical leg, and leaves design R-4 unmet. Fix: add a two-clone test where origin's cursor is advanced out-of-band (X), local ref forced to `from`=C, assert `advanceCursor(from=C)` push is REJECTED and origin stays at X — reddens against `--force` and lease-without-expected.

**CONFIRMED low-severity (both judges, theoretical/suggestion):**
- `to` is never HEX40-validated while `from` is (cursor.mjs:66,90). Safe today (merge-base --is-ancestor + update-ref resolution keep it on a real descendant) but a typo'd/symbolic `to` like HEAD/main advances the cursor to an unintended commit with no diagnostic. Fix: validate `to` with HEX40 (asymmetry closed).
- Non-atomic two-leg advance (cursor.mjs:75-77): local update-ref mutates BEFORE remote push; on remote reject the local ref is left advanced ahead of origin. Self-heals on next `syncCursor` force-fetch; PR1 unused → low impact. Fix: on remote failure restore local to `from`, or push first.

**SUSPECT (single judge, but PROVEN by execution, worth fixing — align with owner-set principles):**
- **window CLI exit-1 off-contract (Judge A, WARNING real).** cursor.mjs:118 — the `window` branch has no try/catch; when `rev-parse HEAD` fails (unborn/detached-corrupt HEAD) Node exits 1 with a stack trace instead of `UNKNOWN`+exit 2. Design §8 CLI contract = window prints PRESENT/ABSENT/UNKNOWN and exits 0/2/2. Once the PR4 wrapper branches on the numeric code, exit 1 maps to the VIOLATION/revert path, not the uncomputable/exit-2 path — a fail-closed INVERSION born in PR1's own CLI (the `accept` branch IS wrapped → exit 1 means something different there). Fix: wrap the window branch in try/catch → `UNKNOWN <msg>` + exit 2.
- **acceptManually echoes `accept: <reason>` BEFORE the CAS (Judge B, WARNING real).** cursor.mjs:99-100 — a stale `from` prints `accept: <reason>` to stdout and THEN throws; the cursor never moved yet an acceptance record was emitted. False audit signal in a governance context. Fix: move the echo below the successful `advanceCursor` return.

**SUGGESTIONS/notes:** CLI `accept <from> --reason x` with missing `to` captures to='--reason' and dies cryptically (reject positional starting with `--`, emit usage); merge-base status 128 folded into "not ancestor" message (distinguish 1 vs 128 for triage); readCursor discards syncCursor status → on fetch failure trusts possibly-stale local instead of returning 'unknown'; hideRefs (`uploadpack.hideRefs refs/governance/`) makes ls-remote return 2 for a ref that EXISTS → false 'absent' → wrong LOUD cursor-missing issue — not GitHub-default but relevant to the m3 GitLab-port thesis (document caveat, prefer fetched-then-rev-parse for absence at port time).

**Proposed fix scope before re-judge (pending owner ruling):** W1 remote-CAS test (doctrine-mandatory), window exit-contract, accept-echo-after-CAS, `to` HEX40 validation. Defer: non-atomic legs (self-heals, unused), CLI parsing polish, merge-base message, hideRefs (port-time). Then re-launch both judges.

Related: [[sdd/issue-259-d2/apply-progress]], [[doctrine/adversarial-test-derivation]], [[decision/issue-259-d2-R1-replacement-tree-effect]].

content:
**Judgment Day Round 1 — PR1 issue-259-d2: code honest, but B5+RACE tests self-confirming on the load-bearing remote CAS**

**What**: Blind dual adversarial review (judgment-day, Judge A + Judge B, both opus) of PR1 of the 5-PR chain for issue-259-d2. Range origin/feature/v2.0.0..HEAD (local, unpushed, HEAD=ec41403). Focus: cursor.mjs + git-seam.mjs (foundation of PR2-PR5). Owner's 3-item brief with mandatory empirical reproduction.

**Why**: Pre-push gate. Owner ruled PR1 must clear judgment-day BEFORE push → my review → human merge → then PR2 starts (PR2 on an unmerged PR1 would anchor to a possibly-broken cursor model — the 8-commit-reset argument again).

**VERDICT: NOT APPROVED (Round 1). One confirmed blocking finding. The CODE is honest; the TESTS are not.**

**CONFIRMED (both judges, both reproduced by MUTATION):**
- B5 (cursor.test.mjs:222) and the acceptManually RACE test (cursor.test.mjs:299) are TAUTOLOGICAL w.r.t. the authoritative remote CAS. The design is remote-authoritative: the ONLY cross-runner protection is the remote `push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<from>` (cursor.mjs:77). But both tests run in a SINGLE working dir, so the second advance throws at the LOCAL `update-ref <ref> <to> <from>` (cursor.mjs:75) BEFORE the push is ever reached. Both judges mutated line 77 to a plain `push --force` (no lease) and showed B5+RACE stay GREEN, while a real two-clone cross-runner race LOSES (stale window overwrites the good cursor). Exactly the self-confirming-test class that burned the prior 8-commit slice. Judge A rated CRITICAL (test integrity), Judge B rated WARNING(real) — same finding, both reproduced. Fix (both judges agree): add a two-clone/cross-runner test where BOTH local refs are C0, one advances, the loser's stale advance is rejected ONLY by the remote lease (local update-ref must be shown to SUCCEED on the loser).

**CLEARED — owner items 1 & 2 both proven HONEST (both judges, reproduced):**
- Item 1 (automatic-path CAS hollow?): NOT hollow. `from` in advanceCursor is a pure caller-supplied parameter, never read internally. Both judges built the real two-clone race (both fetched to C0, both advancing from C0) → remote force-with-lease genuinely REJECTS the stale window, cursor stays at winner's value. The automatic CAS is genuine.
- Item 2 (tri-state ABSENT vs UNKNOWN): HONEST. Fixture-per-failure-mode (bad path, unreachable host/DNS, connection refused, auth denied, malformed URL, https blackhole): every infra failure → git exit 128 → `unknown`. Only reachable-remote-with-ref-genuinely-missing → exit 2 → `absent`. No infra failure maps to ABSENT. B3 test (cursor.test.mjs:102) + git-seam tests are discriminating.

**SUSPECT (Judge A only, but REPRODUCED with commands) — real coupled defect:**
- Human `accept` path is INOPERATIVE on a plain actions/checkout clone. `acceptManually` + CLI `accept` call advanceCursor directly whose FIRST write is the LOCAL CAS `update-ref` (cursor.mjs:75), which needs the governance ref already present locally. A plain checkout never fetches refs/governance/* (per the file's own header comment), so a LEGITIMATE accept with the correct `from`/`to` fails at line 75 before reaching the remote lease. Fails CLOSED (no wrong advance) but renders the sole human escape hatch (design §2.4) unusable on the exact checkout shape. Every accept/advance test masks this by manually running `git update-ref CURSOR_REF from` in the fixture (cursor.test.mjs:237,274,316,394). Becomes CRITICAL if PR2 wires accept on a standalone checkout.

**SUSPECT (one judge each), lower severity:**
- Judge B: advanceCursor's `from` is uncoupled from resolveWindow's base — a PR2 caller written as `advanceCursor({from: readCursor().sha, ...})` would reintroduce hollow CAS (ancestry-theater class). Loose contract = live trap for PR2. WARNING(theoretical) for PR1.
- Judge B: `to` not validated 40-hex (asymmetric with `from`'s HEX40 guard). Not exploitable (execFileSync, no shell; merge-base errors on dash-led arg). WARNING(theoretical).
- Both judges (SUGGESTION): failed remote CAS leaves LOCAL ref advanced (diverged) until next force-fetch syncCursor resets it. Self-heals; harmless in-process because it exits. Caused by the redundant local update-ref (line 75).
- Judge B (SUGGESTION): readCursor has no network timeout — blackholed origin hangs (fail-slow, not fail-wrong; git eventually → 128 → unknown; CI job timeout bounds it).

**ROOT KNOT (my synthesis, for owner ruling)**: the LOCAL `update-ref` at cursor.mjs:75 is the common cause of THREE symptoms — (1) it masks the remote CAS in every test (the confirmed blocking finding), (2) it breaks accept-on-plain-checkout (Judge A suspect), (3) it causes local/remote divergence on lease rejection (both, suggestion). Judge A's stronger fix — DROP the redundant local update-ref and rely solely on the remote --force-with-lease (proven to need no fetched local ref) — kills all three. Minimal alternative — keep line 75, just ADD the two-clone cross-runner test — closes only the confirmed finding and leaves the accept-on-plain-checkout defect live. This is a cursor-MODEL decision (foundation of PR2-PR5), so it needs owner ruling, not an auto-fix.

**Where**: brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/cursor.mjs (lines 26-40 read, 66-79 advance, 75 local CAS, 77 remote CAS, 90-100 acceptManually), cursor.test.mjs (222 B5, 299 RACE), git-seam.mjs (14-27 seam).

**Learned**: Both judges independently reproduced the same tautology by the SAME mutation (line 77 → plain --force) without collaborating — strong signal it is real. content:
**DOCTRINE: "MECANISMO PRESENTE, FUNCIÓN HUECA" — guard-in-wrong-place anti-pattern; mutation-testing is the mechanical bar**

**What**: A named anti-pattern doctrine, established by owner ruling after its THIRD instance in the issue-259-d2 slice. Name: **"MECANISMO PRESENTE, FUNCIÓN HUECA"** (Present Mechanism, Hollow Function).

**The pattern**: a guard/check is structurally PRESENT and looks like protection, but is FUNCTIONALLY HOLLOW because it is evaluated in the wrong PLACE (after the race window it should guard has already moved) or against the wrong AUTHORITY (a local cache instead of the remote source of truth). It passes exactly when it should fail.

**The three instances in this slice (one pattern, not isolated incidents):**
1. **Ancestry check to PROVE A REVERT** (F3): `merge-base --is-ancestor offender candidate` to "prove candidate reverts offender" — but on a linear main every later commit is a descendant, so it proves what is ALWAYS true. Wrong authority: ancestry cannot prove a tree effect.
2. **acceptManually CAS** (owner-ruled fix): read `from` internally via readCursor() a microsecond before the swap → CAS reasserts the ref's current value. Wrong place.
3. **Local CAS in advanceCursor** (cursor.mjs:75, removed): `update-ref REF to from` fired BEFORE the remote `push --force-with-lease` (the real authority) → a MASK. Wrong authority: local ref is not the source of truth.

**CRITICAL NUANCE — do NOT over-generalize (owner ruling, Round 2 PR1):** "ancestry is theater" was ONLY about instance 1 — using ancestry to PROVE A REVERT. Ancestry is a LEGITIMATE, healthy guard for ORDERING. The `merge-base --is-ancestor(from → to)` check in advanceCursor/acceptManually exists to enforce FORWARD-ONLY (prevent the cursor moving backward), and for THAT it works correctly. Same tool, different purpose: VALID for "is `to` later than `from`?", INVALID for "was the offender reverted?". Do NOT let the F3 lesson generalize until it deletes a sound ordering guard. Corollary of ordering: the ancestry check runs BEFORE the ref update, so a well-formed-but-non-commit sha (e.g. a tree/blob OID) fails CLOSED at merge-base before any write.

**MECHANICAL DETECTION — the standard instrument from now on**: MUTATION TESTING. Mutate the guard (e.g. `--force-with-lease` → `--force`; make merge-base always succeed; read `from` internally; drop a HEX40 validation). If the tests stay GREEN, the guard is hollow and/or the test is self-confirming. This is the mechanical form of the house bar "a test must go RED against the plausible-but-wrong fix, not just against un-fixed code." Any test that CLAIMS to protect an invariant MUST be validated by mutating the mechanism it protects and observing RED. Proven in Round 2: two blind judges independently re-ran the bar (force-with-lease→force AND lease-value corruption) and confirmed RED — that is what upgraded the fix from "claimed fixed" to "verified fixed".

**Why**: Self-confirming tests are worse than no tests — they convert "unverified" into "verified green" while the hole stays open. Burned the monolithic 8-commit slice (reset) and re-appeared on the new load-bearing invariant in PR1's B5/RACE tests.

**How to apply**: (1) For any guard, ask "before or after the authority/race it defends?" and "checking the source of truth or a cache?" — but FIRST ask "what is this guard's actual purpose?" (ordering vs proof vs CAS); a guard valid for its real purpose is NOT theater. (2) For any protective test, mutate the protected mechanism and require RED. (3) Prefer moving decision logic to the single authority over layering local guards that can mask it. See [[sdd/issue-259-d2/judgment-round-1-pr1]], [[sdd/issue-259-d2/judgment-round-2-pr1]].

content:
**DOCTRINE (Track H reviewer-protocol): a cold reviewer's DIFFERENT ENVIRONMENT is an instrument, not an accident — env-dependent green is invisible to same-env reviewers**

**What**: A reviewer-independence doctrine, established when the external cold-clone reviewer (CP-PR1) caught a blocker on issue-259-d2 PR1 that the author AND both blind judgment-day judges had all missed.

**The blind spot**: B6 (cursor.test.mjs) depended on AMBIENT git identity. `makeBareOriginAndClone` cloned into `cloneDir` without setting `user.name`/`user.email` (unlike the house `makeRepo` helper), and B6 commits on an orphan branch there. With no configured identity AND no auto-detectable identity (a fresh runner / a machine without a passwd gecos), that commit fails; `headSha` silently returned `''`; `readCursor` parsed an empty sha and returned `{state:'unknown'}` with no reason → the assertion failed ONLY off the author's machine. On gandalf (global git identity present) it passed 29/29 for everyone.

**Why three reviewers missed it**: the author and both judges all ran on gandalf, which HAS global git identity. They shared not just a repo but an ENVIRONMENT. A test that passes only in the environment of whoever wrote it is a class no same-environment reviewer can detect — no amount of adversarial reading or local mutation-testing surfaces it, because the hidden dependency is on ambient config, not on the code under review.

**THE DOCTRINE (for Track H reviewer-protocol.md — file does NOT exist yet, create when Track H materializes)**: "El entorno distinto del revisor es un instrumento, no un accidente." Reviewer coldness is not only "not sharing the author's working memory / mental model" — it is ALSO **not sharing the author's ambient environment** (git config, installed tools, env vars, OS identity, locale, filesystem layout). A genuinely cold review runs in a DIFFERENT environment on purpose, because environment-dependent green is precisely the failure class that a same-environment reviewer — human or AI judge — structurally cannot see.

**Mechanical instrument**: run the suite under a HOSTILE environment that strips the ambient assumption. For git identity: `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file with user.useConfigOnly=true> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` — this forces git to demand explicit identity, reproducing a cold runner. Reproduced the B6 RED under exactly this harness (23/24), then fixed and confirmed 29/29 green under the same harness. Generalize: any test asserting behavior should be run once in a deliberately foreign environment before it is trusted.

**The fix (PR1)**: `setIdentity()` on every clone (cloneDir + every plainClone), matching the house `makeRepo` pattern; harden `headSha` to THROW a diagnostic error instead of fabricating `''` when a sha-producing git step fails, so the same silent-masquerade can never recur (second-order fix — a failing sha producer must scream, not fabricate).

**CI note**: `.github/workflows/governance.yml` runs `npm test` with `actions/checkout@v4` and sets NO git identity — it passed only because GitHub-hosted runners have an ambient auto-detectable identity. The hermeticity fix removes that dependency; do NOT "fix" it by adding `git config` to CI (that masks non-hermetic tests instead of eliminating the dependency).

**Relation to the other doctrine**: [[governance/doctrine-present-mechanism-hollow-function]] is about a guard in the wrong place/authority; THIS is about a test with a hidden environmental dependency. Both are "green that doesn't mean what it claims." Mutation-testing catches the first; a foreign-environment run catches the second. See [[sdd/issue-259-d2/apply-progress]].

content:
**Judgment Day Round 1 — PR2 issue-259-d2 NOT APPROVED: tree-effect predicate forgeable by RENAME (path-scoped, blind to relocation)**

**What**: Blind dual adversarial review (both opus) of PR2 (resolution.mjs, tree-effect revert-resolution predicate), commit 49fd4dd on feat/issue-259-d2-pr2-tree-effect-resolution. The design calls this predicate "the entire security thesis" and says PR2 exists to answer ONE question: can it be forged? Answer: **YES.**

**VERDICT: NOT APPROVED. One CRITICAL, both judges, both reproduced empirically.**

**CONFIRMED CRITICAL — RENAME/MOVE bypass (both judges, independent repros):**
- resolution.mjs isResolvedAt (~:48-57) is PATH-SCOPED: `P = changedPaths(offender)`, `D = paths changed between offender^1 and tip`, `resolved ⟺ P ∩ D = ∅`. But the design §3.1 claims tree-effect proves "the offender's payload is NOT on disk" — a CONTENT claim. These diverge under a rename.
- Attack: offender M ADDS payload at path P (the dominant governance shape — adds an ADR/payload). A later ordinary commit does `git mv P P2` (content byte-identical, blob OID preserved). Now on path P the tree is absent at M^1 AND absent at tip → P ∉ D → P ∩ D = ∅ → `{resolved:true}` while the identical payload is still on disk at P2. Both judges reproduced with real resolution.mjs in scratch repos (generic payload AND the exact adrPresence-ungoverned-ADR class).
- The `--no-renames` flag (module comment claims it's the rename defense) only applies to changedPaths(M) — the offender's OWN diff. It does NOT protect the offender^1..tip comparison; for add-then-rename it actively LEAKS (the baseline M^1 never had P, so no rename pair is visible regardless of detection).
- Fails OPEN in NORMAL operation too, not only under attack: a legitimate later refactor that renames a file an un-accepted offender added will auto-resolve that offender and advance the cursor past it.
- Second manifestation (same root cause): isReverterOf (~:69-72) is built on the same predicate, so a pure rename commit satisfies BOTH clauses (isResolvedAt(M,cand)=true AND isResolvedAt(M,cand^1)=false) → the rename is crowned as M's "reverter" and, in PR3's reverter-skip, would itself be [SKIP]ped — the laundering commit clears M AND exempts itself.
- Fixture coverage gap: A1–A6 (design §7.1) have ZERO rename fixture (`rg "git mv|rename"` → none), despite --no-renames being the headline defense. §7.1's threat model omits relocation entirely. Per doctrine #900, the missing attack shape is a coverage defect.

**Root cause / fix direction (needs OWNER ruling — changes design §3.2, the security thesis):** the predicate proves "path P unchanged", not "content gone". To be forge-proof it must prove the CONTENT the offender introduced is absent at tip, not that its original paths are untouched. Candidate fix: BLOB-OID approach — the set of blob OIDs the offender introduced (present in M, absent in M^1); resolved iff none of those blob OIDs appear anywhere in tip's tree. A rename preserves the blob OID → caught. False-positive (identical bytes elsewhere) fails CLOSED (stays flagged → human accept). Rejected alternative already in design §3.1: inverted-diff (brittle). Rename-detection on M^1..tip does NOT fix it (baseline never had P). This is a design-§3.2 change.

**Theoretical WARNING (Judge B) — root/parentless offender:** `${rev}^1` on a root commit → git exit 128 → gitOrThrow THROWS (uncaught) rather than returning a structured `{resolved:false}`/uncomputable. Fails CLOSED at this layer (never resolves), but whether it stays fail-closed end-to-end depends on the PR3 caller (brain-audit.mjs) catching the throw → exit-2. Unreachable for real offenders (--first-parent --merges always have ^1). Flag for PR3 wiring.
